summary: Map the existing Kirigami/QML stoandl-gui app (features, UI structure, D-Bus surface, infra) to prepare a GTK4/libadwaita rewrite

result.component: App shell — Main.qml (ApplicationWindow, NavigationTabBar, showTab, page instantiation), DaemonPlaceholder.qml (daemon-down empty state), StatusChip.qml (status pill). Backed by src/StoandlClient.cpp/.h for daemonUp/startDaemon.
result.purpose: The application shell: a single convergent (Plasma Mobile + desktop) Kirigami ApplicationWindow that hosts a 5-destination tab bar (Watch/Health/Apps/Notifications/Settings), swaps the root page per tab, hides all navigation and shows a reusable "daemon not running" placeholder when the stoandl daemon is down, and provides two shared UI primitives used app-wide: a passive-notification toast helper and a small status pill (StatusChip).
features: Kirigami.ApplicationWindow titled 'stoandl' with a fixed minimum size (22x30 gridUnits) and a default size (30x48 gridUnits); gridUnit-relative sizing, no hardcoded pixels.

Five navigation destinations in a Kirigami.NavigationTabBar: Watch (tab 0, the launch view), Health (1), Apps (2), Notifications (3), Settings (4). KDE HIG rule: <=5 destinations => tab bar, not a drawer.

Each tab has a symbolic icon (chronometer-symbolic, love-symbolic, view-list-icons-symbolic, notifications-symbolic, settings-configure-symbolic) + a text label; actions are checkable and checked-bound to root.currentTab.

Tab bar placed in the window FOOTER intentionally so it renders BELOW content on mobile (narrow) and relocates ABOVE content on desktop (wide) — Kirigami's responsive footer behavior; this is the convergence mechanism.
Both globalDrawer and contextDrawer are explicitly set to null — navigation is exclusively the responsive tab bar, no hamburger/drawer.

showTab(index): re-tapping the ACTIVE tab pops all pushed sub-pages back to that tab's root (pageStack.depth>1 -> pop loop, then return). Switching to a DIFFERENT tab first pops all sub-pages, sets currentTab, then pageStack.replace()s the root page component in place.
currentTab is an int property (default 0 = Watch) that is the single source of truth for which destination is active and which tab action shows as checked.
pageComponents is a readonly array of 5 Component ids (watchComponent..settingsComponent) indexed by tab number; showTab replaces with pageComponents[index].

Initial page is an INLINE WatchPage {} assigned to pageStack.initialPage (NOT the watchComponent Component) — deliberate: assigning a Component makes Kirigami createObject() it with a transient null parent and Qt6 warns 'Created graphical object was not placed in the graphics scene'. The inline page is parented into the window tree at construction so it is silent. watchComponent is still used by showTab's replace() for later navigation.
Whole tab bar is hidden (visible:false) AND collapsed (height:0) when StoandlClient.daemonUp is false — nothing in the app works without the daemon, so navigation disappears entirely when it is down.

DaemonPlaceholder.qml: a reusable Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage empty state ('stoandl daemon not running' + explanation) that each page embeds (visible: !StoandlClient.daemonUp) rather than living in the shell; the shell only hides the nav.

DaemonPlaceholder offers a helpfulAction 'Start daemon' (media-playback-start-symbolic) that calls StoandlClient.startDaemon() (systemctl --user start stoandl) and toasts either 'Starting stoandl…' on success or a failure message.

StatusChip.qml: a small non-interactive status/flag pill (Rectangle, pill-shaped radius:height/2) with a `label` string and a `tint` color; background is tint at 15% alpha, border is tint at 50% alpha, label text uses tint color and Kirigami.Theme.smallFont; sized to its label + spacing.

Global toast pattern: every page defines `function toast(msg){ applicationWindow().showPassiveNotification(msg) }` — passive notifications are the app-wide transient feedback mechanism, provided by the ApplicationWindow shell.
result.uiStructure: Root is Kirigami.ApplicationWindow. It contains a pageStack (Kirigami page-row/stack) whose initialPage is an inline WatchPage; navigation swaps the single root page via pageStack.replace() and pushes focused sub-pages via pageStack.push() (e.g. from SettingsPage). The window footer holds a Kirigami.NavigationTabBar with 5 Kirigami.Action entries (icon+text, checkable). No global/context drawer. Pages are declared as 5 QML Components (WatchPage, HealthPage, AppsPage, NotificationsPage, SettingsPage) referenced by an array. DaemonPlaceholder is a standalone Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage (icon, text, explanation, helpfulAction) embedded per-page, centered as an empty state. StatusChip is a standalone Rectangle-based pill with a centered QQC2.Label. Toasts are Kirigami passive notifications overlaid on the window (transient banners at the bottom).
dbusOrClientCalls: StoandlClient.daemonUp (Q_PROPERTY bool, NOTIFY daemonUpChanged) — read to gate tab-bar visibility (shell) and per-page content vs placeholder. Backed by NameHasOwner('de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control') probe (recheckDaemon) + NameOwnerChanged watcher (onNameOwnerChanged).

StoandlClient.startDaemon() (Q_INVOKABLE bool) — QProcess::startDetached('systemctl', ['--user','start','stoandl']) since the daemon is NOT D-Bus-activated; returns whether launch succeeded and schedules recheckDaemon() at 1500ms and 4000ms as fallback to NameOwnerChanged. Called by DaemonPlaceholder's Start-daemon action.
daemonUpChanged() signal — pages connect onDaemonUpChanged to re-run their reload() when the daemon comes back up (the shell just re-shows the nav via the visible binding).
applicationWindow().showPassiveNotification(msg) — Kirigami/QML built-in (not D-Bus), used by DaemonPlaceholder and the per-page toast() helpers for transient feedback.
interactions: Tap a tab in the NavigationTabBar -> showTab(index): switches destination (pops sub-pages + replaces root) or, if already active, pops back to that tab's root.
Re-tap the currently-active tab -> pops any pushed detail sub-page(s) to return to the tab root (a way 'back' without a back button on mobile).
Tap 'Start daemon' in the DaemonPlaceholder -> attempts systemctl --user start stoandl and shows a toast ('Starting stoandl…' or the failure message).
Resize/rotate the window (convergence) -> the footer NavigationTabBar automatically relocates below (mobile/narrow) vs above (desktop/wide) the content.
Daemon goes down/up (external) -> tab bar hides/reappears reactively; pages swap between DaemonPlaceholder and content.
Passive notification toasts appear transiently and auto-dismiss (Kirigami default) after mutating actions across the app.
states: daemon UP: tab bar visible, pages show real content.
daemon DOWN: tab bar hidden AND height-collapsed to 0; each page independently shows DaemonPlaceholder (visible:!daemonUp) with a Start-daemon action.
Active-tab state: currentTab drives which tab Action is checked (visual selection).
Sub-page pushed vs root: pageStack.depth>1 means a detail page is on top of a tab root; showTab pops these.
StatusChip is purely presentational — its shown/hidden and label/tint are decided by the embedding page (e.g. active/system/SOON/Quarantined/Crashed); no internal state.
Toasts are transient/ephemeral (no persistent state in the shell).
signalsConsumed: daemonUpChanged (StoandlClient) — the ONLY reactive signal the shell itself consumes, via the tab bar's `visible: StoandlClient.daemonUp` binding. (The seven daemon Control signals — WatchesChanged/FirmwareProgress/LockerChanged/LanguageProgress/ExtensionsChanged/ExtensionStateChanged/CalendarsChanged — are handled inside StoandlClient/individual pages, not the shell.)
result.gnomeMappingNotes: "Kirigami.ApplicationWindow -> Adw.ApplicationWindow (or Gtk.ApplicationWindow) with an Adw.ToastOverlay as its top-level child so any page can raise Adw.Toast (the GTK equivalent of showPassiveNotification/toast()). The 5-destination NavigationTabBar maps to an Adw.ViewStack driven by an Adw.ViewSwitcher: put the switcher in the header bar on wide layouts and use an Adw.ViewSwitcherBar in the bottom of an Adw.ToolbarView on narrow layouts — this reproduces the footer-below-on-mobile / header-above-on-desktop responsive behavior automatically (Adw.Breakpoint can toggle switcher reveal). Alternatively wrap in Adw.NavigationSplitView/Adw.ViewSwitcher; but ViewStack+ViewSwitcher (top+bar) is the closest 1:1 to a convergent tab bar. Each tab's icon+label maps to an Adw.ViewStackPage (icon-name + title). Hiding the whole nav when the daemon is down: bind the ViewSwitcher(Bar) visibility to a daemonUp property; or, cleaner in GTK, keep a top-level Adw.ViewStack with two pages — one 'main' (the switcher UI) and one 'placeholder' — and switch to the placeholder when daemonUp is false. showTab's push/pop of detail sub-pages maps to Adw.NavigationView (per-tab) with Adw.NavigationPage children: pageStack.push -> navigationView.push(); re-tap-active-tab-pops-to-root -> navigationView.pop_to_tag()/pop() (and GTK gives a real back button in the Adw.HeaderBar, so the re-tap-to-go-back affordance is less critical). pageStack.replace of the whole root is unnecessary — each tab is its own persistent NavigationView inside a ViewStackPage. DaemonPlaceholder (Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage with icon/text/explanation/helpfulAction) -> Adw.StatusPage (icon-name, title, description) with a suggested-action Gtk.Button child ('Start daemon'); or an Adw.Banner if shown inline atop content. The systemctl offer/toast maps to spawning the process (Gio.Subprocess) and raising an Adw.Toast on the ToastOverlay. StatusChip (small tinted pill) has no direct Adw widget — build a Gtk.Label with a CSS pill class (border-radius, tinted background/border via a CSS provider derived from a theme accent/state color); do NOT hardcode colors, derive from the GTK theme/accent like the Kirigami.Theme roles here (positiveTextColor -> success, disabledTextColor -> dim/label styleclass). Toasts: showPassiveNotification -> adw_toast_overlay_add_toast(new Adw.Toast). gridUnit-relative sizing -> just set default/min size in px but prefer natural sizing; Adw handles adaptive layout via breakpoints instead of manual gridUnit math."
gotchas: The initialPage MUST be an inline `WatchPage {}`, NOT the `watchComponent` Component — assigning a Component causes Kirigami to createObject() with a transient null parent and emit the Qt6 'Created graphical object was not placed in the graphics scene' warning; deferring via onCompleted/Qt.callLater does NOT fix it (it's the Component indirection, not timing). In GTK this concern disappears (pages are just added to the ViewStack), but note the intent: tab 0 must be constructed/present at startup.

showTab distinguishes two cases off the SAME tap: index===currentTab -> only pop sub-pages (return early, do NOT replace); index!==currentTab -> pop sub-pages THEN replace root. Preserve both behaviors: switching tabs must also drop any pushed detail page, not just swap the root.

The tab bar is both `visible:false` AND `height:0` when down — hiding alone would leave layout space in the footer; the height collapse is deliberate. Replicate by fully removing/hiding the switcher bar, not just opacity.

Daemon-down handling is split: the SHELL only hides the nav; each PAGE embeds its own DaemonPlaceholder (visible:!daemonUp) and shows/hides its real content. So the placeholder is per-page, reused via the DaemonPlaceholder component, not a single shell-level screen. A GTK rewrite could centralize this (one placeholder page in a top ViewStack) since the nav is hidden anyway.

The daemon is NOT D-Bus-activated: never assume it starts on demand. startDaemon() shells out to `systemctl --user start stoandl` and re-probes NameHasOwner at 1500ms/4000ms as a fallback to the NameOwnerChanged watcher — the button's boolean return only means the launch was spawned, not that the daemon is up.

StatusChip is intentionally non-interactive (a flag/pill), tint defaults to disabledTextColor; alpha values 0.15 (fill) / 0.5 (border) are the density spec — keep the low-alpha tinted look. Colors come only from Kirigami.Theme roles (positiveTextColor for 'active', disabledTextColor for 'SOON'/system), never hardcoded — mirror with GTK theme/state classes.

Toasts are accessed via applicationWindow().showPassiveNotification — a window-scoped built-in every page relies on through a local `toast()` helper; in GTK this must be a shared Adw.ToastOverlay reachable from every page (e.g. via the application window), otherwise the per-page toast() helpers have nowhere to post.

pageStack.replace (not push) is used for tab roots so the back-stack never accumulates tab roots — only within-tab detail pages are pushed. Keep tab switching non-stacking in the rewrite (separate NavigationView per tab).

result.purpose: The launch view for the stoandl Pebble GUI. It lists paired/known watches, surfaces the active watch's connection/Bluetooth status and battery, drives the pairing flow (including numeric-code confirm/decline), shows firmware update banners and inline flash progress, and hosts a per-watch details dialog (hardware facts, nickname rename, developer connection toggle, language pack install, changelog link, and a debug/recovery submenu incl. local .pbz firmware flash).
features: Live watch list from ListWatches
Active-watch hero card tappable to details
Numeric-code pairing confirm/decline
Firmware update banner + inline flash progress
Local .pbz sideload flash with confirmation
Details dialog with debug/recovery submenu and language install
Nickname rename
Developer connection toggle
Ring watch / Forget watch / Factory reset / Reboot to recovery
result.uiStructure: WatchPage is a Kirigami.ScrollablePage (title 'Watch') whose sole child is a spacing:0 ColumnLayout of conditionally-visible sections stacked top-to-bottom: DaemonPlaceholder (daemon down), a Bluetooth-off Kirigami.InlineMessage(Warning), a Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage no-watch empty state (with a 'Pair new watch' helpfulAction), the firmware flash-progress FormHeader+FormCard(FormTextDelegate+ProgressBar), the update-available Kirigami.InlineMessage(Information) with inline actions, the 'Active watch' FormHeader + FormCard containing a tappable AbstractFormDelegate hero (RowLayout: icon huge / name+StatusChip column / battery column / chevron), and the 'Known watches' FormHeader + FormCard with a Repeater of AbstractFormDelegate rows (icon / name+subtitle column / active chip / Connect button / forget ToolButton). Page actions live on the page `actions` array (Kirigami renders header on desktop, footer toolbar on mobile). Custom components referenced: DaemonPlaceholder, StatusChip. Dialogs are Kirigami.PromptDialog (pair, forget) and a WatchDetailsDialog. WatchDetailsDialog is a Kirigami.Dialog (bottom sheet on mobile / popup on desktop) with preferredWidth ~25 gridUnits, standardButtons Close, and an internal `view` state machine ('main'|'debug'|'language') implemented as three mutually-exclusive visible ColumnLayouts inside one ColumnLayout (the title changes per view; sub-views have a 'Back' ActionRow). Reusable inline components: DetailRow (label/value, optional mono) and ActionRow (QQC2.ItemDelegate with icon, danger tint, chevron, 'SOON' chip). Nested PromptDialogs: rename, reboot-to-recovery, factory-reset (type-to-confirm), fwFlashConfirm; plus a QtQuick.Dialogs FileDialog.
dbusOrClientCalls: StoandlClient.refreshWatches() — re-fetch ListWatches; called after every mutation (connect/unpair/pair-success/rename) and on Sync now / daemonUp
StoandlClient.startWatchPoll() / stopWatchPoll() — start/stop the 20s BluetoothStatus + missed-WatchesChanged safety poll, tied to page lifetime (Component.onCompleted/onDestruction)

StoandlClient.checkFirmware() — CheckFirmware; returns {kind, latest, updateAvailable, changelogUrl}; drives the update banner and is re-run on daemonUp, Sync now, details 'What's new' and 'Check for updates'
StoandlClient.updateFirmware() — UpdateFirmware; starts a network firmware flash; handles ok / uptodate / other kinds via toast
StoandlClient.sideloadFirmware(QUrl fileUrl) — SideloadFirmware(path) with the local .pbz absolute path; the risky local flash
StoandlClient.connectWatch(name) — ConnectWatch; toast on !ok then refresh
StoandlClient.pair() — Pair; then startPairPoll() on ok
StoandlClient.repair(name) — Repair; then startPairPoll() on ok
StoandlClient.confirmPairing(bool accept) — ConfirmPairing(accept) for the numeric-compare Accept/Decline
StoandlClient.startPairPoll() / stopPairPoll() — 1.5s/145s-ceiling pairing status poll (started on pair/repair ok, stopped onClosed)
StoandlClient.unpair(name) — Unpair; toast on !ok then refresh
StoandlClient.findWatch() — FindWatch (async, 20s timeout); rings the watch; result via onFindWatchResult(ok)
StoandlClient.watchDetails() — WatchDetails -> ok:name\tcode\tmodel\tplatform\ttransport\tfirmware\tserial\tbattery\tlastSync
StoandlClient.setWatchNickname(name, nickname) — SetWatchNickname; rename
StoandlClient.devConnectionStatus() — DevConnectionStatus; returns {active, ...}
StoandlClient.startDevConnection() / stopDevConnection() — StartDevConnection (returns {kind, port}) / StopDevConnection
StoandlClient.listLanguages() — ListLanguages; rows {id, displayName, source, installed}
StoandlClient.installLanguage(id) — InstallLanguage(query=id)
StoandlClient.takeScreenshot() — TakeScreenshot(path) -> {kind, path}
StoandlClient.getCoreDump() — GetCoreDump(path) -> {kind ok|none, path, msg}
StoandlClient.gatherLogs() — GatherLogs(path) -> {kind, path, msg}
StoandlClient.supportBundle('') — CLI shell-out (not D-Bus); async result via onCliResult(op='support', ok, message)
StoandlClient.resetIntoRecovery() — ResetIntoRecovery (reboot to PRF)
StoandlClient.factoryReset() — FactoryReset

Signals consumed via Connections: onWatchesChanged(rows), onPairStatus(kind,msg), onFindWatchResult(ok), onFirmwareStatus(kind,percent,detail), onDaemonUpChanged(), onLanguageStatus(kind,percent,detail), onCliResult(op,ok,message)
StoandlClient.daemonUp / bluetoothOn — reactive properties gating visibility and action enablement
Qt.openUrlExternally(changelogUrl) — opens firmware changelog in the browser
applicationWindow().showPassiveNotification(msg) — all toasts
interactions: Tap 'Pair new watch' action -> pair dialog opens, calls Pair, polls, may reach confirm:<code>
In confirm state: read the large monospace code, tap Accept (ConfirmPairing(true)) or Decline (ConfirmPairing(false)); dialog goes to 'pending' with 'Completing…/Declining…'
Cancel/close pair dialog stops the pair poll
Tap a disconnected known-watch row OR its 'Connect' button -> ConnectWatch
Tap the forget ToolButton (row) or details 'Forget watch' -> forget confirm dialog -> Forget/Cancel
Tap the hero card -> open WatchDetailsDialog (fetches WatchDetails + dev status + languages)
Tap 'Ring watch' action -> FindWatch, toast 'Ringing watch…' / 'No watch ready to ring'
Tap 'Sync now' -> refresh + checkFirmware + 'Refreshed' toast
Tap 'Update now' in banner -> UpdateFirmware; 'What's new' -> open changelog URL
Details: toggle Developer connection switch (optimistic, reverts on failure)
Details: tap Language -> language sub-view; tap an uninstalled pack -> InstallLanguage (progress via LanguageProgress/onLanguageStatus toasts)
Details: Rename watch… -> prefilled dialog, Rename enabled only when non-empty
Details: Capture screenshot / Check for updates -> toast
Details: Debug… -> debug sub-view; Back returns to main
Debug: Core dump / Pull watch logs / Support bundle (async CLI) toasts
Debug: Reboot to recovery -> Ok/Cancel confirm -> ResetIntoRecovery
Debug: Flash firmware from file… -> FileDialog (*.pbz) -> named confirm -> SideloadFirmware -> closes details to show progress banner
Debug: Factory reset -> type 'yes' to enable the destructive button -> FactoryReset
'Write notification' debug row is disabled with a 'SOON' chip
states: daemon down: DaemonPlaceholder shown, nav/actions gated by daemonUp
Bluetooth off (daemonUp && !bluetoothOn): Warning InlineMessage; Pair action disabled
no-watch empty (daemonUp && bluetoothOn && no connected && empty list): PlaceholderMessage with Pair action
firmware idle vs busy (fwPhase '' vs downloading/waiting/inprogress/notready) -> fwBusy drives the progress card; percent<0 => indeterminate ProgressBar
firmware update available (fwInfo.kind==ok && updateAvailable) -> banner
firmware flash terminal: success/failed/timeout toasts clear state
pairing states: '' or 'pending' -> BusyIndicator; 'confirm' -> code + Accept/Decline; 'error'/'timeout' -> error icon; 'ok' -> toast+close
watch row connected vs disconnected (icon tint, subtitle, active chip vs Connect button)
language pack installed vs not (highlight + checkmark; current shown on Language row; '—'/'English (US)' fallbacks)
details fact rows show '—' when a field is empty
language install terminal: success (reloads languages) / failed / disconnected toasts
dev-connection toggle active/inactive with revert-on-failure
GetCoreDump 'none' -> 'No core dump available'
signalsConsumed: WatchesChanged -> onWatchesChanged(rows) -> applyWatches (re-derives connectedWatch)
FirmwareProgress/FirmwareStatus -> onFirmwareStatus(kind,percent,detail) -> pushes phase/percent or terminal toast
LanguageProgress/LanguageStatus -> onLanguageStatus(kind,percent,detail) -> toasts + reload on success (details dialog)
PairStatus -> onPairStatus(kind,msg) -> pairDialog.handleStatus (confirm/ok/error/timeout)
FindWatchResult -> onFindWatchResult(ok) -> toast
CliResult -> onCliResult(op,ok,message) -> support-bundle toast
daemonUpChanged -> onDaemonUpChanged() -> refreshWatches + checkFirmware
20s watch safety poll (startWatchPoll) carrying BluetoothStatus and covering a missed WatchesChanged
1.5s pair poll (startPairPoll, 145s ceiling) for pairing status
result.gnomeMappingNotes: Page: Kirigami.ScrollablePage -> AdwPreferencesPage inside an AdwToolbarView (AdwHeaderBar for title + actions) wrapped by an AdwNavigationView so the details 'dialog' can instead be an AdwNavigationPage push on desktop; the three page actions become AdwHeaderBar buttons (GtkButton with icon-name), with the primary/pair action possibly in a header GtkMenuButton or as a suffix. FormCard.FormHeader+FormCard sections -> AdwPreferencesGroup (title = header). AbstractFormDelegate hero + known-watch rows -> AdwActionRow (activatable, with a leading GtkImage icon, title/subtitle, and suffix widgets: a battery label, a GtkButton 'Connect', an icon GtkButton for forget, and a GtkImage go-next for the activatable hero). StatusChip -> a small GtkLabel with a .success/.dim CSS class (or Adw pill styling). DaemonPlaceholder / PlaceholderMessage (no watch) -> AdwStatusPage (icon + title + description + a suggested-action button). Bluetooth-off InlineMessage(Warning) and update-available InlineMessage(Information) -> AdwBanner (with a button-label + revealed) or an inline GtkInfoBar; the update banner's two actions map to a Banner button plus a secondary link button (or a small action row). Firmware flash-progress FormCard -> an AdwPreferencesGroup containing a GtkProgressBar (pulse() when indeterminate) with a status GtkLabel. Pair dialog (Kirigami.PromptDialog) -> AdwAlertDialog (or AdwDialog): the confirm:<code> state shows a large monospace GtkLabel and two responses ('decline'/'accept', accept as suggested), busy state = GtkSpinner, error = error icon; use adw_alert_dialog_add_responses + set_response_appearance. Forget/recovery/factory confirms -> AdwAlertDialog with a destructive response; factory-reset type-'yes' -> AdwAlertDialog containing an AdwEntryRow whose changed handler enables the destructive response (adw_alert_dialog_set_response_enabled). WatchDetailsDialog (Kirigami.Dialog, adaptive sheet/popup) -> best as an AdwNavigationView of AdwNavigationPages (main/debug/language) presented in an AdwDialog (or a bottom sheet AdwDialog on mobile), so the internal view state machine becomes real navigation pushes with a back button in each AdwHeaderBar. DetailRow fact rows -> AdwActionRow with title + a dim suffix GtkLabel (monospace via a 'monospace' CSS class for serial). ActionRow -> AdwActionRow (activatable) or AdwButtonRow; danger rows use the .error CSS class; chevron rows use AdwActionRow's default go-next; the 'SOON' chip -> a suffix pill label + row set insensitive. Developer connection -> AdwSwitchRow (with subtitle). Language row -> AdwActionRow showing current value + chevron; the language picker list -> AdwPreferencesGroup of activatable AdwActionRows with a check icon suffix on the installed one (or an AdwComboRow if a simple picker suffices, though the install-on-select + progress semantics favor explicit rows). Rename dialog -> AdwAlertDialog with an AdwEntryRow. FileDialog for .pbz -> Gtk.FileDialog (open) with a Gtk.FileFilter for *.pbz. All toasts (showPassiveNotification) -> adw_toast_overlay_add_toast(AdwToast) on a top-level AdwToastOverlay. Qt.openUrlExternally -> Gtk.UriLauncher / gtk_show_uri. No charts here, so no Gtk.DrawingArea needed.
gotchas: connectedWatch is derived, not authoritative: applyWatches loops ListWatches and picks the FIRST row with connected==true; there is no separate connected-watch call
Every mutating call is followed by an explicit refreshWatches() — the WatchesChanged signal is only a best-effort poke, the re-fetch is authoritative (project hard rule)

PairStatus 'confirm' carries the code in the msg field (kind==='confirm', msg=code); it is a NUMERIC-COMPARISON pairing (user visually matches code on watch), not a code-entry field — never render an input
Pair poll must be stopped onClosed (stopPairPoll) or it keeps polling; success closes the dialog and toasts

Firmware phase vocabulary is shared with FirmwareStatus: downloading/waiting/inprogress/notready are non-terminal; success/failed/timeout are terminal and reset fwPhase/fwPercent (success also clears fwInfo so the banner disappears)
ProgressBar is indeterminate when fwPercent < 0 (fwPercent initial -1)
SideloadFirmware receives a QUrl that the client converts to an absolute daemon-side path; the local flash confirm derives the display filename by splitting the URL on '/' and decodeURIComponent
On successful sideload the details dialog closes itself so the WatchPage's flash-progress banner (driven by FirmwareProgress) becomes visible — progress lives on the page, not the dialog
battery/transport are STRINGS that may be empty ('') — UI guards with !== '' and appends '%' manually; treat empty as unknown, not zero
Details fields are all optional and fall back to '—'; currentLang falls back to '—' then to the installed pack's displayName, reset before scanning so a stale pack isn't shown
Developer-connection switch is optimistic: it flips the model on ok and REVERTS checked to dialog.devOn on failure
Factory reset uses type-'yes' (case-insensitive, trimmed) to enable the destructive button; reboot-to-recovery uses a plain Ok/Cancel
Support bundle is NOT a D-Bus call — it shells out to the stoandl CLI and reports asynchronously via CliResult(op=='support'); the immediate toast is just 'Building support bundle…'
'Write notification' debug action is intentionally disabled with a 'SOON' chip

The details dialog is a single Kirigami.Dialog that swaps between three visible-gated ColumnLayouts and changes its title per view; a GTK rewrite should model this as real navigation to avoid the collapse workaround (Layout.preferredWidth pinned to 25 gridUnits) noted in the source
checkFirmware() only runs when daemonUp; changelog 'What's new' actions re-call CheckFirmware on demand rather than reusing fwInfo (details dialog does its own CheckFirmware)
Ring watch action requires a connected watch (connectedWatch !== null); FindWatch is async with a 20s timeout because it rings until a button press

result.component: Health tab — /workspace/qml/HealthPage.qml (single-file slice; includes inline components StatTile, HrStat, SleepLegend, MetricBars). Depends on external QML components DaemonPlaceholder and StoandlClient (C++ shim).
result.purpose: A read-only health dashboard mirroring the official Pebble app's HealthTimeRange model. One period selector (Daily/Weekly/Monthly) plus one navigator drive all three metric sections (Steps, Sleep, Heart rate): Daily renders rich per-day cards (hourly step bars, a light/deep sleep timeline, a minute-level HR line chart); Weekly/Monthly render per-day bar charts. The only mutation is an explicit "Sync health" page action; everything else is polled/parsed in C++ and only rendered by QML.
features: Period type switcher with 3 mutually-exclusive checkable buttons: Daily (periodType='day'), Weekly ('week'), Monthly ('month'). Switching type resets periodOffset to 0 and reloads.

Period navigator: prev ('go-previous-symbolic' = Earlier, increments offset) / center bold label / next ('go-next-symbolic' = Later, decrements offset). Offset 0 = current period. Clamped by maxOffsetFor: day max 30, week max 12, month max 11.
Prev button disabled at max offset; next button disabled at offset 0 (can't go into the future).

periodLabel() computes the center label locally in JS: day → 'Today'/'Yesterday'/'ddd d MMM'; week → 'This week' or 'd MMM – d MMM' span; month → 'This month' or 'MMMM yyyy'. Must match daemon's windows.
STEPS section (always present when hasData): headline = stepsTotal (day) or stepsAvgPerDay (period), unit 'steps'/'avg / day', plus 'Typical N' when stepsTypical>0.
Steps Daily: hourly step MetricBars (hourly=true, 24 bars, 12a/6a/12p/6p time axis) + three StatTiles (Distance km, Calories kcal, Active min).
Steps Weekly/Monthly: per-day MetricBars with a faint 'typical' refLine (=stepsTypical) + a 'Total N over M days' footnote (stepsTotal / daysWithData).
SLEEP section (present when hasData): headline = fmtMin(sleepTotalMin) (day: total 'asleep', period: 'avg / night'); day-only bedtime→wakeup clock range (fmtClock).

Sleep most-recent-night fallback: on the Today card, if the shown night's wake date != the navigated day, shows 'Last recorded night · <span>' (sleepNightSpan gives 'Di–Mi' bedtime→wake weekday span, else the date). Detected purely from summary.sleepWakeup, no extra D-Bus field.
Sleep empty states: no totalMin → 'No sleep data yet.' (offset 0) / 'No sleep recorded for this day.' (day) / 'No sleep recorded for this period.'

Sleep Daily timeline: a rounded track (subtle text-tinted background) over a 6PM→noon window with light/deep colored segments from sleepSegments [{start,width,deep}], plus a 4-tick time axis (6 PM / 12 AM / 6 AM / noon).
Sleep Weekly/Monthly: per-night stacked MetricBars (light band + darker deep base) with y-axis in hours (valueToHeight: min→hours, labels 'Nh').
Sleep legend (day only): Deep + Light SleepLegend dots with fmtMin totals; typical shown as 'Typical Hh MMm' (day) or 'Typical … / night' footnote (period), only when sleepTypicalMin>0.
Deep vs Light colors: light = highlightColor, deep = Qt.darker(highlight,1.6). Both SOLID so 'deep darker than light' holds in both light and dark themes (a translucent tint would invert on dark bg).

HEART RATE section (only rendered when hrAvailable): stat row Resting · Average · Min · Max. Resting is primary/large when hrResting>0, else Average is primary. Min/Max come from daily minute samples so day-only; week/month shows Resting+Average.
HR empty state: day with hrStats.count===0, or week/month with hrAvg<=0 → 'No heart-rate data for <period>.' (real HRM-capable months can have no readings).

HR Daily: minute-level HR line chart (Canvas) with gradient area fill under the line, a left bpm y-axis (3 gridlines + min/mid/max tick labels), and a 5-tick time axis (12AM/6AM/12PM/6PM/12AM). Single-sample degenerate case draws a dot.
HR Weekly/Monthly: per-day average-HR MetricBars, negativeTextColor tint, floorAtMin=true (bars read from a non-zero floor).

MetricBars reusable chart: 3-tick left y-axis (0/50/100% of range), optional refLine (typical), valueToHeight rescale, floorAtMin (HR) vs niceCeil rounding (zero-floored), stacked deep sub-bar, faded main bar, sparse x labels (labelEvery = ceil(len/8)) or hourly time axis.
Empty/placeholder handling: DaemonPlaceholder when daemon down; PlaceholderMessage 'No health data yet' when up but no data, with a 'Sync health' helpful action.
hrStats computed in QML from heartSamples: count/min/max/avg (rounded).
result.uiStructure: Kirigami.ScrollablePage (objectName 'health', title 'Health'). Page `actions` has one Kirigami.Action 'Sync health' (view-refresh-symbolic, enabled only when daemonUp) — Kirigami places it in the header on desktop / footer toolbar on mobile. Page `header` is a QQC2.ToolBar (visible only when daemonUp; height collapses to 0 when hidden) containing a ColumnLayout: row 1 = 3 fill-width autoExclusive checkable Buttons (Daily/Weekly/Monthly via Repeater); row 2 = RowLayout with prev ToolButton, centered bold fill-width Label (periodLabel), next ToolButton. The scrolling body is a single ColumnLayout (spacing 0) holding: DaemonPlaceholder, Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage (no-data), then three repeating (FormCard.FormHeader + FormCard.FormCard) blocks for Steps / Sleep / Heart rate. Each FormCard wraps a single AbstractFormDelegate (background:null) whose contentItem is a ColumnLayout of headline RowLayout + charts + stat tiles + labels. FormHeaders carry a trailing Kirigami.Icon (view-statistics-symbolic / weather-clear-night-symbolic / love-symbolic). Charts are built from Repeaters of Rectangles (bars, sleep segments, gridlines) and one QtQuick Canvas (HR line, repainted on heartSamplesChanged and Theme.colorsChanged). Inline components: StatTile (value over label, centered), HrStat (heading number + 'bpm' over label, primary=large+accent), SleepLegend (round dot + name + bold minutes), MetricBars (Item chart with gutter y-axis + RowLayout of bar cells + a bottom RowLayout of sparse labels).
dbusOrClientCalls: StoandlClient.daemonUp (property) — gate all rendering; drives placeholder vs content and header/action enablement.

StoandlClient.healthSummary(periodType, periodOffset) → summary object (kind 'ok' + ~20 fields: stepsTotal, stepsAvgPerDay, stepsTypical, daysWithData, distanceKm, kcal, activeMin, sleepDeepMin, sleepLightMin, sleepTotalMin, sleepTypicalMin, sleepBedtime(epoch), sleepWakeup(epoch), hrAvailable(bool), hrResting, hrAvg). Maps to GetHealthSummary daemon call.
StoandlClient.stepsBars(periodType, periodOffset) → [{label,value,typical,hasValue}] hourly buckets (day) or per-day bars (week/month). Maps to GetHealthSeries('steps',...).
StoandlClient.sleepTimeline(periodType, periodOffset) → [{start,width,deep}] daily segments (day only).
StoandlClient.heartSamples(periodType, periodOffset) → [{minute,bpm}] daily minute-level (day only, only fetched when hrAvailable). Maps to GetHealthSeries('heart',...).
StoandlClient.sleepBars(periodType, periodOffset) → [{label,value(totalMin),deep,hasValue}] (week/month only).
StoandlClient.heartBars(periodType, periodOffset) → [{label,value(avgBpm),hasValue}] (week/month only, only when hrAvailable).

StoandlClient.syncHealth() → {ok, kind, tail} — the sole mutation. On ok toast 'Syncing health data…'; kind 'notready' → 'No watch connected'; tail contains 'not enabled' → 'Health sync is disabled — enable it in Settings'; else 'Health: <tail|kind>'. Always reload() after.
StoandlClient signal onDaemonUpChanged → reload() when daemon comes up (Connections block). Component.onCompleted → reload().
signalsConsumed: StoandlClient.daemonUpChanged (Connections) → reload() when daemon becomes up.
page.heartSamplesChanged → hrCanvas.requestPaint() (repaint HR line when data changes).
Kirigami.Theme.colorsChanged → hrCanvas.requestPaint() (repaint HR line on theme/palette change).

Implicit reactive re-render: all charts/labels are bound to the property snapshots (summary, sleepSegments, heartSamples, stepBarData, sleepBarData, heartBarData) which reload() reassigns — no other polling here (C++ owns polling).
states: daemon down → DaemonPlaceholder, header hidden (height 0), Sync action disabled.
daemon up + no data (summary.kind !== 'ok') → Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage 'No health data yet' with Sync helpful action; the three metric cards hidden.
daemon up + hasData → metric sections shown.
Sleep: haveSleep false → text empty state ('No sleep data yet.'/'…for this day.'/'…for this period.'); timeline/bars/legend hidden.
Sleep fallback: Today card showing an earlier recorded night → 'Last recorded night · <span>' banner-label.
Heart rate: hrAvailable false → entire HR section (header+card) not rendered.

Heart rate: hrAvailable true but no samples (day count 0) or hrAvg<=0 (week/month) → 'No heart-rate data for <period>.' empty label; stat row and chart hidden. (An HRM-capable past month with no readings still shows this.)
HR single-sample degenerate → Canvas draws a dot instead of a line.
Toast/passive-notification states from syncHealth: syncing / no watch / disabled / generic error.
interactions: Tap Daily/Weekly/Monthly button → setPeriodType (resets offset to 0, reload).
Tap Earlier (prev) ToolButton → setPeriodOffset(offset+1), clamped; tooltip 'Earlier', Accessible.name 'Earlier'.
Tap Later (next) ToolButton → setPeriodOffset(offset-1), clamped ≥0; tooltip 'Later', Accessible.name 'Later'.
Trigger 'Sync health' page action (header/footer) → syncHealth() → toast + reload.
Trigger 'Sync health' from the no-data PlaceholderMessage helpful action → syncHealth().
Hover prev/next → ToolTip shown.
No per-row/inline actions, no dialogs, no confirmations — this is a read-only dashboard; the only feedback channel is passive-notification toasts.
result.gnomeMappingNotes: Page shell: Kirigami.ScrollablePage → AdwNavigationPage wrapping a Gtk.ScrolledWindow over an AdwClamp/GtkBox; page title in an AdwHeaderBar. The 'Sync health' page action → a Gtk.Button in the AdwHeaderBar (icon view-refresh-symbolic), no FAB. Passive-notification toasts → AdwToast via an AdwToastOverlay wrapping the page content. Pinned header ToolBar (period switcher + navigator) → put it in the AdwHeaderBar or a second toolbar row (Adw uses AdwHeaderBar + optionally a bottom bar via AdwToolbarView top/bottom bars; AdwToolbarView is the natural container so content scrolls under the pinned toolbars). The 3-way Daily/Weekly/Monthly autoExclusive button group → an AdwViewSwitcher backed by an AdwViewStack (three stack pages), or a GtkBox of linked toggle buttons with the 'linked' style class (Adw.ViewSwitcher is the idiomatic segmented control). The prev/label/next navigator → a GtkBox with two flat GtkButtons (icons go-previous/go-next-symbolic) flanking a bold centered GtkLabel; sensitivity toggled like the enabled bindings. FormCard.FormHeader + FormCard.FormCard → AdwPreferencesGroup (group title = header, trailing icon → the group's header-suffix widget) containing rows; but since these cards hold custom charts rather than list rows, use AdwPreferencesGroup with a single content child that is a GtkBox (or an unstyled AdwActionRow acting as a container). Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage 'No health data yet' → AdwStatusPage (icon love-symbolic, title, description, and a suggested-action Gtk.Button 'Sync health'). DaemonPlaceholder (daemon-down) → another AdwStatusPage, or an AdwBanner at the top offering 'systemctl --user start stoandl'. StatTile / HrStat / SleepLegend → plain GtkBox composites (GtkLabel stacks; the round swatch dot → a small GtkDrawingArea or a CSS-styled GtkBox). All charts (MetricBars bar charts, sleep timeline track+segments, sleep/step/HR axes, and the Canvas HR line with gradient fill) → Gtk.DrawingArea with a Cairo draw_func; the Canvas gradient fill maps to cairo linear gradient + stroke path; repaint (requestPaint) → queue_draw() on data/theme change. Theme roles: Kirigami.Theme.highlightColor/negativeTextColor/textColor/disabledTextColor/smallFont → GTK style-context accent color / error color / CSS-driven colors and Pango small font; keep 'never hardcode' by reading theme colors (gtk_widget_get_color / named CSS colors like @accent_color, @error_color) in the draw_func. Empty-state inline labels stay as dim GtkLabels (dim-label style class). Signals: daemonUpChanged / heartSamplesChanged / Theme.colorsChanged → GObject signal handlers / property notifies that call queue_draw() and reload(). No AdwComboRow/AdwSpinRow/AdwExpanderRow/AdwEntryRow needed here (read-only dashboard, no form inputs).
gotchas: Offset clamping is asymmetric per type: day 0..30, week 0..12, month 0..11 (maxOffsetFor). Prev disabled at max, next disabled at 0 — never navigate into the future.
Switching period TYPE resets offset to 0; switching offset keeps type. periodLabel() is computed in JS and MUST match the daemon's window boundaries or labels will mislead.

hrAvailable (watch has an HRM) is distinct from having readings: gate the whole HR SECTION on hrAvailable, but gate the stat row/chart vs empty-state on hrStats.count>0 (day) / hrAvg>0 (week/month). A real HRM-capable past month can have zero readings.
heartSamples/heartBars are only fetched when hrAvailable — reload() short-circuits them to [] otherwise (avoids useless D-Bus calls).
Deep sleep color MUST be a solid Qt.darker(highlight,1.6), NOT an opacity of the light tint — a translucent tint composites darker on a dark background and would invert deep/light in dark theme.

Sleep data is inherently a night-or-more behind (watch hands each night's overlay over late, consume-once). The Today card falls back to the most recent recorded night; fallback is detected purely from summary.sleepWakeup date != navigated day — single source of truth, no extra D-Bus field.
sleepNightSpan strips the locale's trailing '.' on weekday abbreviations (regex /\.$/) and collapses same-day bedtime/wake to a single weekday.
Sleep timeline window is fixed 6 PM → noon (18h span); segment start/width are fractions of that window, min bar width Math.max(2, …).

MetricBars y-axis: floorAtMin=true (HR) floors at the actual series min so the bottom tick is a real bpm value; otherwise floors at 0 and rounds the top to a 'nice' ceiling (niceCeil: 1/1.2/1.5/2/2.5/3/4/5/7.5/10 × 10ⁿ) so labels read cleanly.
Sleep bars pass valueToHeight (min→hours) so both the bar heights AND the y-tick labels ('Nh') are in hours while values remain minutes; deep sub-bar is stacked at the base.
x-axis label thinning: hourly=true labels only 12AM/6AM/12PM/6PM (indices 0/6/12/18); otherwise labelEvery = ceil(len/8) — sparse labels for month.
hasValue distinguishes a real 0 from missing data — a bar with hasValue=false renders height 0 (gap), not a 2px stub.
The HR Canvas must requestPaint() on BOTH heartSamplesChanged and Theme.colorsChanged (the stroke/gradient read theme colors); missing the theme connection leaves stale colors after a theme switch.
fmtK compact axis: ≥10000 → 'Nk' (rounded), ≥1000 → 'N.Nk', else raw. fmtMin → 'Hh MMm' (zero-padded minutes). fmtClock: epoch≤0 → '—', else 12h AM/PM.

The QML scope gotcha noted project-wide (bindings in nested inline Components can't call page methods) is sidestepped here by passing formatLabel/valueToHeight as function properties and reading only modelData.* / bars.* inside delegates.
Every mutating call (only syncHealth here) is followed by reload() — the D-Bus/signal is a best-effort poke, the re-fetch is authoritative.
The header ToolBar collapses height to 0 (not just visible:false) when daemon down so it doesn't reserve space.

result.purpose: A single ScrollablePage that manages the watch's installed content across three segments — watchfaces, watchapps, and host-side extensions — plus the daemon's app "locker". It lists items with icons/metadata, lets the user launch/configure/remove apps and enable/configure/uninstall extensions, and sideload new .pbw apps or extension archives from disk.
features: Three-way segment switch (Faces / Apps / Extensions) pinned in a header toolbar, each label showing a live count (e.g. 'Faces · 3'), driven by page.segment ('faces'|'apps'|'ext')
Single ListApps snapshot (page.apps) is filtered in QML into faces (a.isFace) and others (!a.isFace); extensions are a separate ExtList snapshot (page.extensions)

Faces/Apps rows (reusable AppRow component): lazily-loaded extracted menu-icon PNG (file:// from StoandlClient.appIcon(uuid)) rendered at integer 2x with smoothing OFF to keep hard pixel edges; falls back to a themed glyph (starred-symbolic if active, preferences-desktop-theme-symbolic if a face, application-x-executable-symbolic otherwise)
Row title = app.title; subtitle = developer (or uuid fallback) optionally suffixed with ' · v'+version when version known
'active' StatusChip (positive tint) shown on the currently-running face/app (appData.active === true); active glyph also switches to a highlighted star icon
Per-app inline Settings button (configure-symbolic) shown only when appData.config === true
Per-app inline Delete-from-locker button (edit-delete-symbolic) shown only when appData.system !== true (system apps cannot be removed)
Tapping an app row launches it (doLaunch); the config/delete buttons consume the click so they don't also launch
Extension rows (FormSwitchDelegate): text=name, description composed from author · vVersion — manifest description, switch state = enabled

Extension runtime-state chip from ExtensionStateChanged: 'Quarantined' (negative tint) when runtimeState==='quarantined', 'Crashed (restarting)' (neutral tint) when runtimeState==='exited'; hidden for normal running/stopped
Per-extension Settings button shown only when hasConfig === true; dispatches to a URL open or a schema-driven form depending on ext.config ('url'|'schema')
Per-extension Uninstall button (always shown) opening a confirm dialog with a 'Keep configuration' checkbox (default checked)
Install action is segment-aware: 'Install .pbw' (faces/apps) vs 'Install extension' (extensions); a Refresh action re-reads the locker + extensions
Extension footnote FormTextDelegate explaining extensions are host-side notification companions (only when list non-empty)

Schema-driven extension config dialog: renders one control per schema field by type (bool→switch, string→text field w/ password echo when secret, int→spin box, enum→combo box), collects values by field key on Save
result.uiStructure: Kirigami.ScrollablePage (title 'Apps & Faces'). header is a QQC2.ToolBar (position Header, height collapses to 0 when daemon down) containing a RowLayout of three checkable/autoExclusive fill-width QQC2.Buttons acting as a segmented control with counts. Page-level actions[] = two Kirigami.Action (segment-aware Install + Refresh), rendered by Kirigami in the header (desktop) / footer toolbar (mobile). Body is a ColumnLayout(spacing 0): a DaemonPlaceholder (custom, when daemon down); three Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage empty states (no faces / no apps / no extensions, each with a helpfulAction that opens the relevant file dialog); three FormCard.FormCard sections each with a Repeater — Faces (AppRow), Apps (AppRow), Extensions (FormSwitchDelegate with a trailing RowLayout of StatusChip + config ToolButton + delete ToolButton); and a trailing FormCard.FormTextDelegate footnote. AppRow is a FormCard.AbstractFormDelegate whose contentItem is a RowLayout: icon Item (Image over Kirigami.Icon fallback) + ColumnLayout(title label + small dimmed subtitle label) + StatusChip + config ToolButton + delete ToolButton. Dialogs: two Kirigami.PromptDialog (remove app confirm, uninstall ext confirm with a CheckBox), one Kirigami.Dialog (schema config form: a FormCard.FormCard with a Repeater of AbstractFormDelegate rows switching control by field type), two QtQuick.Dialogs.FileDialog (pbw install, extension archive install). Custom reused components: StatusChip, DaemonPlaceholder.
dbusOrClientCalls: StoandlClient.refreshApps() — re-fetch ListApps (locker snapshot); called on load, on daemonUp, after launch/remove/sideload, and by Refresh
StoandlClient.refreshExtensions() — re-fetch ExtList; called on load, on daemonUp, after enable/disable/uninstall/config-save/install, and by Refresh
StoandlClient.launchApp(uuid) — launch a face/app; returns {ok, tail, kind}; toasts and re-fetches apps (launching a face flips the active flag)
StoandlClient.removeApp(uuid) — delete an app from the locker; returns {ok, tail, kind}; re-fetches apps
StoandlClient.openConfig(uuid) — open a watchapp's config webview; returns {kind ('ok'|'none'|other), opened, msg}; ok+opened → browser toast, none → 'is the app running on the watch?' toast
StoandlClient.appIcon(uuid) — resolve a cached extracted menu-icon PNG path (file:// URL or empty); called lazily per AppRow on completion
StoandlClient.extEnable(name) / extDisable(name) — toggle an extension; returns {kind}; re-fetches extensions
StoandlClient.extOpenConfig(name) — open an extension's URL settings (ext.config==='url'); returns {kind, opened, msg}
StoandlClient.extConfigSchema(name) — fetch schema field descriptors (array of {key,label,type,options,secret}) for the schema config dialog
StoandlClient.extGetConfig(name) — fetch current config values ({values:{key→val}}) for the schema dialog
StoandlClient.extSetConfig(name, valuesObject) — save collected schema form values; returns {kind}; re-fetches extensions
StoandlClient.extUninstall(name, keepConfig:bool) — stop + remove an extension, optionally keeping config; returns {kind}; re-fetches extensions
StoandlClient.extInstall(absolutePath) — install an extension archive (.tar.gz/.tgz/.tar/.zip); returns {kind}; re-fetches extensions
StoandlClient.sideloadApp(absolutePath) — install a .pbw; returns {ok, tail, kind}; re-fetches apps
StoandlClient.daemonUp / onDaemonUpChanged — gates nav/actions/content and triggers reload() when the daemon comes up

Signals consumed via Connections: onAppsChanged(rows) → page.apps; onExtensionsChanged(rows) → page.extensions (backed by ListApps polling + ExtensionsChanged/ExtensionStateChanged; ExtensionStateChanged surfaces as modelData.runtimeState)
result.gnomeMappingNotes: Page/segments: the pinned header segment switcher maps to an AdwViewSwitcher bound to an AdwViewStack with three pages (Faces/Apps/Extensions), placed in the AdwHeaderBar (or AdwViewSwitcherBar in the bottom bar on mobile for convergence); the live counts don't fit AdwViewSwitcher titles cleanly, so either use a Gtk.Box of Gtk.ToggleButtons in a 'linked' style class (matching the current three-checkable-buttons approach with count labels) or drop counts. Overall page: AdwToolbarView with an AdwHeaderBar; the page-level Install/Refresh actions become AdwHeaderBar buttons (Install split by active stack page). Lists: each FormCard.FormCard → AdwPreferencesGroup (inside an AdwPreferencesPage), or a Gtk.ListBox with class 'boxed-list'. AppRow → AdwActionRow (title/subtitle built-in), with the menu icon as a leading Gtk.Image/Gtk.Picture rendered from a Gdk.Texture with interpolation disabled / exact-integer scaling for the pixel-art icons, the fallback glyph as a themed icon-name; the 'active' chip as a suffix Gtk.Label with a pill/accent CSS class; Settings and Delete become flat suffix Gtk.Buttons with tooltips. Row-click-to-launch → AdwActionRow activatable=true with an activated handler (suffix buttons don't propagate activation). Extension row → AdwSwitchRow (title/subtitle + built-in switch) with suffix Gtk.Buttons for Settings/Uninstall and the runtime-state chip as a suffix Gtk.Label with error/warning CSS classes. Empty states (Kirigami.PlaceholderMessage) → AdwStatusPage (icon + title + description + a helpful Gtk.Button), shown by swapping the AdwViewStack page child or via a Gtk.Stack. Daemon-down placeholder → AdwStatusPage (or an AdwBanner across all tabs). Toasts (showPassiveNotification) → AdwToast via an AdwToastOverlay wrapping the window content. Confirm dialogs (remove app, uninstall ext) → AdwAlertDialog with responses (Cancel/Delete, Delete marked destructive); the uninstall 'Keep configuration' checkbox → a Gtk.CheckButton in the AdwAlertDialog's extra_child. Schema config dialog → an AdwDialog/AdwPreferencesDialog with an AdwPreferencesGroup whose rows are generated per field: bool→AdwSwitchRow, string→AdwEntryRow/AdwPasswordEntryRow (password when secret), int→AdwSpinRow, enum→AdwComboRow (Gtk.StringList model, selected from current value); Save/Cancel as header/response buttons. File pickers → Gtk.FileDialog (async open) with Gtk.FileFilter for .pbw and the archive extensions. StatusChip → a Gtk.Label with a rounded 'pill'/'tag' CSS class tinted via 'accent'/'error'/'warning' classes. No charts here, so no Gtk.DrawingArea needed.
interactions: Tap a Faces/Apps/Extensions segment button → switch page.segment (autoExclusive toggles)
Tap an app/face row → doLaunch: launchApp(uuid), toast 'Launched X' or 'Launch failed: …', re-fetch apps

Tap a row's Settings (configure-symbolic) button → doConfig: openConfig(uuid); toasts 'Opening config in your browser…' / 'No config available — is the app running on the watch?' / 'Config unavailable: …' (does not launch the row)
Tap a row's Delete button → removeConfirm.openFor(app): PromptDialog with Delete/Cancel; Delete → removeApp, re-fetch
Toggle an extension switch → extToggle: extEnable/extDisable, toast on failure, re-fetch extensions
Tap an extension Settings button → configureExt: if config==='url' extOpenConfig + toast; if config==='schema' open extConfigDialog.openFor(name); else 'No settings for …' toast

Tap an extension Uninstall button → uninstallConfirm.openFor(name): dialog with 'Keep configuration' checkbox (default checked) + Uninstall/Cancel; Uninstall → extUninstall(name, keepConfig), toast, re-fetch
In the schema config dialog: edit switch/text/spin/combo controls, tap Save → extSetConfig(name, collect()), toast 'Saved …' / 'Save failed: …', re-fetch; or Cancel/close button
Tap Install action → opens pbwFileDialog (faces/apps segment) or extFileDialog (ext segment); on accept → sideloadApp/extInstall with the selected absolute path, toast, re-fetch
Tap Refresh action → reload() (refreshApps + refreshExtensions) + 'Refreshed' toast
Tap an empty-state helpfulAction button → opens the relevant install file dialog
states: daemon down → DaemonPlaceholder shown, header toolbar collapses (height 0) and actions disabled (StoandlClient.daemonUp gates everything)
Faces empty (daemon up, segment faces, faces.length 0) → PlaceholderMessage 'No watchfaces' / 'Install a .pbw to get started.'
Apps empty → PlaceholderMessage 'No apps' / 'Install a .pbw to get started.'
Extensions empty → PlaceholderMessage 'No extensions installed' with the host-side companion explanation
Populated list per segment → FormCard with rows (visible gated on daemonUp + segment + length>0)
app.active === true → 'active' chip + highlighted star icon
app.config === true → Settings button visible; app.system === true → Delete button hidden
extension runtimeState 'quarantined' → red 'Quarantined' chip; 'exited' → neutral 'Crashed (restarting)' chip; otherwise no chip
extension hasConfig === true → Settings button visible; config kind 'url' vs 'schema' vs none decides the settings behavior
app icon: resolved PNG (Image.Ready) vs generic themed glyph fallback while empty/unavailable
call result kinds handled: ok / none / other-error via r.kind/r.ok/r.tail/r.msg surfaced in toasts
signalsConsumed: StoandlClient.onAppsChanged(rows) → refresh page.apps (backed by ListApps polling; no dedicated LockerChanged handler wired in QML — comment notes 'no LockerChanged signal yet', so re-fetch after every mutation)
StoandlClient.onExtensionsChanged(rows) → refresh page.extensions (backed by ExtensionsChanged poke + per-extension ExtensionStateChanged runtimeState merged into rows in C++)
StoandlClient.onDaemonUpChanged → reload() when daemon comes up
Component.onCompleted → reload() (initial fetch on show)
gotchas: Icon rendering is deliberately pixel-exact: menu bitmaps are ~25px black-on-white; Image uses smooth:false and renders at integer 2x (min(implicitWidth*2, parent.width)) — a naive GTK scale with interpolation would mangle them; preserve nearest-neighbor / exact-integer scaling.
Config/Delete ToolButtons must consume the click so the row's onClicked (launch) does NOT also fire — in GTK, suffix buttons on an activatable AdwActionRow already stop activation, but verify.
Faces vs Apps split is done in QML via an a.isFace filter on a single ListApps snapshot — one data source, two derived views; extensions are a separate snapshot.
'active' state means the currently-running face/app; launching re-fetches because the active flag moves.
System apps cannot be removed (Delete hidden when app.system===true); mirror by hiding/disabling the destructive action in GTK.

Extension config has THREE modes keyed off ext.config: 'url' (open external settings), 'schema' (in-app generated form via extConfigSchema/extGetConfig/extSetConfig), and none ('No settings' toast) — hasConfig gates button visibility, config kind gates behavior.

Schema dialog collect() reads live control values via fieldRepeater.itemAt(i).fieldKey/fieldValue keyed by field key; fieldValue is compared loosely (checked === true || === 'true'; parseInt for int) — replicate loose typing when reading daemon values.
String schema field uses password echo only when modelData.secret is set.
Uninstall keepConfig defaults to TRUE (checked) each time the dialog opens (reset in openFor).
runtimeState chip only distinguishes quarantined/exited; normal running/stopped are intentionally chip-less — the switch conveys enabled state, not run state.
File paths passed to sideloadApp/extInstall are absolute daemon-side paths (daemon is co-located); keep that assumption.

After every mutation the code re-fetches (refreshApps/refreshExtensions) even though signals exist — the signal is a best-effort poke, the re-fetch is authoritative; preserve this belt-and-suspenders pattern.
The header ToolBar collapses to height 0 (rather than merely hidden) when the daemon is down so it takes no layout space.
Toasts are the only feedback for success/failure of every action (showPassiveNotification), including the exact messages — map faithfully to AdwToast.

result.purpose: The Notifications tab controls how phone notifications are forwarded to the Pebble watch: a master forward on/off switch, a temporary mute-all (30m/1h/today/resume), a per-app list (each app opens a deeper dialog with mute controls, a vibration style radio list, and a custom-icon combo), and a regex filter list (allow/block) with an add-filter prompt. Everything is polled/re-fetched via reload() since this slice has no change signal — every mutation re-fetches its slice per the handoff hard rules.
features: Master 'Forward notifications' switch — reflects whether the 'notifications' service is enabled in the sync-status table; toggling calls setSyncEnabled('notifications', bool)
Temporary mute-all with three presets (30 min / 1 hr / Today) shown when not all-muted; a single 'Resume now' button shown when all apps are currently muted
allMuted is DERIVED (not fetched): true only when apps.length>0 AND every app.muted===true — there is no NotifGetMuteAll getter, the daemon reflects mute-all into each app's mute state

Per-app list: one row per notifList() record showing app name, an inline On/Off switch, a subtitle ('Muted' or 'Vibration · <vibe>'), a bell icon tinted highlight (active) or disabled (muted), and a go-next chevron
Per-app row On/Off switch: On means NOT muted; toggling calls notifSetMute(name, 'never'|'always'); the switch consumes the click so the row's open-dialog onClicked does not also fire
Tapping a per-app row opens the per-app deeper dialog (appDialog)
Per-app dialog: on/off switch + temp-mute presets (30m/1h/today) or Resume, mirroring the master mute controls but scoped to one app

result.purpose: The Settings area is a category landing (a short list of category rows) that pushes five focused sub-pages onto the navigation stack: Sync (per-service master toggles + force-sync), Calendars (CalDAV/iCal/.ics source CRUD with nested per-calendar toggles), Watch settings (~46 WatchPrefs rendered one delegate per type), Daemon configuration (curated stoandl.conf keys, schema-driven), and Backup & diagnostics (backup/restore/support bundle via the CLI). This is the KDE-HIG pattern for a large settings surface: don't put everything on one scroll.
features: Settings landing: 5 category rows (Sync; Calendars; Watch settings; Daemon configuration; Backup & diagnostics), each with an icon, a text label, and a one-line description, that push a focused sub-page onto the page stack (a back button/extra column appears)
Every page shows a DaemonPlaceholder (daemon-not-running state) when StoandlClient.daemonUp is false, and hides its real content; every page re-syncs on daemonUpChanged when the daemon comes back
Sync page: 'Services' section — one master on/off switch per sync service (weather, calendar, music, health, dnd), with 'notifications' explicitly filtered OUT (it lives on the Notifications tab)
Sync page: each service switch shows a 'Last sync · <time or never>' description, is disabled when the service is unavailable (available === false), and reflects enabled state
Sync page: 'Sync now' section — force-sync buttons for the three pull services (Weather, Calendar, Health); a page-level 'Sync all now' header action runs all three sequentially
Sync page: a 'Manage calendars…' button that pushes the Calendars sub-page
Calendars page: master 'Auto-discover local calendars' toggle (reads/writes config key calendar.discover; finds desktop .ics like Calindori, ~/.calendars; 'No egress')

Calendars page: sources grouped into one card per account; each account card shows an icon, label/url subtitle, and per-source Edit/Remove inline buttons (only for real sources, not the synthetic 'Discovered & other' group)

Calendars page: each account's discovered calendars nested below its header as per-calendar enable switches; orphan/discovered calendars (no matching source) collected into a read-only 'Discovered & other' group
Calendars page: empty-state PlaceholderMessage ('No calendars yet') with an 'Add calendar' helpful action when there are no sources and no groups
Calendars page: per-source 'No calendars found yet' hint text (CalDAV variant mentions checking URL/username/password)

Calendars page: Remove confirmation dialog warning that calendars, their watch pins, and the stored CalDAV password will be deleted

Watch settings: number spinbox uses ~100 steps across min/max, shows a unit via textFromValue, and debounces writes ~500ms so a step/auto-repeat drag doesn't storm the daemon or recreate the focused control mid-drag

Watch settings: color row shows a circular swatch of the current hex + a 'Choose…' preset combo; no preselection because current is a hex, not a preset name; FormColorDelegate deliberately avoided (it calls i18ndc/KF6)
Watch settings: empty-state PlaceholderMessage ('No watch settings' / 'Connect a watch…') when daemon up but no prefs

Daemon configuration page: schema-driven — each curated stoandl.conf key rendered by declared type (toggle→switch, combo→combobox, else→text field); new daemon keys appear automatically; changes apply live (no restart)
Daemon configuration page: empty-state PlaceholderMessage ('No configuration') when schema is empty; explanatory footer text otherwise
Backup page: 'Back up now' button (full backup of watch + daemon state)
Backup page: 'Restore from file…' button opening a native file picker (accepts *.tar/*.tar.gz/*.tgz/*.zip)
Backup page: 'Create support bundle' diagnostics button
Backup page: results reported asynchronously via cliResult(op, ok, message) — immediate 'Backing up…'/'Restoring…'/'Building support bundle…' toast, then a completion/failure toast
result.uiStructure: All six are Kirigami.ScrollablePage with a title and an objectName. Content is a top-level ColumnLayout(spacing:0) holding FormCard.FormCard groups (rounded cards) separated by FormCard.FormHeader section titles and FormCard.FormDelegateSeparator between rows. Landing (SettingsPage): one FormCard with FormButtonDelegate rows (icon.name + text + description + arrow), a Component per sub-page, and page.open() → applicationWindow().pageStack.push(). Sync: FormHeader 'Services' + FormCard with a Repeater of FormSwitchDelegate; FormHeader 'Sync now' + FormCard of FormButtonDelegate; a trailing FormCard with the 'Manage calendars…' button; one Kirigami.Action ('Sync all now') on the page. Calendars: a master toggle FormCard; a PlaceholderMessage; a Repeater over computed 'groups' where each group is a FormCard whose header is an AbstractFormDelegate (RowLayout: Kirigami.Icon + ColumnLayout of two labels + two QQC2.ToolButton edit/remove with tooltips) followed by a separator and a Repeater of FormSwitchDelegate per calendar, plus a FormSectionText empty hint; a Kirigami.Dialog (add/edit form of FormComboBoxDelegate + FormTextFieldDelegate x3, custom Save/Cancel footer actions, showCloseButton) and a Kirigami.PromptDialog (remove confirm with custom Remove/Cancel actions); two page actions (Add, Sync now). WatchSettings: PlaceholderMessage + a Repeater over computed 'sections' where each is a ColumnLayout of FormHeader + FormCard whose Repeater uses a Loader per pref selecting one of six inline Components (boolPref/enumPref/quickPref/numberPref/colorPref/fallbackPref); the color component is a hand-built AbstractFormDelegate (RowLayout: label column + Rectangle swatch + QQC2.ComboBox). General: a FormCard with a Repeater→Loader per schema key picking cfgToggle/cfgCombo/cfgText inline Components, a PlaceholderMessage, and a FormSectionText footer. Backup: FormHeader 'Backup' + FormCard (two FormButtonDelegate), FormHeader 'Diagnostics' + FormCard (one FormButtonDelegate), plus a QtQuick.Dialogs.FileDialog for restore. Toasts are applicationWindow().showPassiveNotification(). Icons are freedesktop symbolic names; spacing via Kirigami.Units; no hardcoded colors/fonts (Kirigami.Theme roles).

result.gnomeMappingNotes: Overall: the settings landing + pushed sub-pages map to an AdwPreferencesDialog/AdwPreferencesWindow with an AdwNavigationView (or the built-in subpage stack), or an AdwNavigationView of AdwNavigationPages if kept in the main window. Landing category rows (FormButtonDelegate icon+text+description+arrow) → AdwActionRow with an icon prefix and a go-next symbolic suffix, activatable, in an AdwPreferencesGroup on an AdwPreferencesPage. FormHeader section titles → AdwPreferencesGroup title. FormCard groups → AdwPreferencesGroup. FormSwitchDelegate → AdwSwitchRow. FormComboBoxDelegate → AdwComboRow (with a Gtk.StringList model; for enum/quicklaunch set selected by index). FormSpinBoxDelegate → AdwSpinRow (with a Gtk.Adjustment for min/max/step; unit shown via custom formatting or a suffix — note AdwSpinRow lacks textFromValue so append the unit in a label/format; keep the 500ms debounce with a GLib timeout source, resetting on ::value-changed). FormTextFieldDelegate → AdwEntryRow (password field → AdwPasswordEntryRow). The color row (swatch + preset combo) → an AdwActionRow with a Gtk.DrawingArea or a small styled widget as the color swatch prefix plus an AdwComboRow (or a GtkColorDialogButton if free-form color were wanted, but here presets → AdwComboRow of preset names). The nested account cards (header row + per-calendar toggles + edit/remove buttons) → AdwExpanderRow (title/subtitle + suffix Gtk.Buttons for edit/remove) whose child rows are AdwSwitchRows per calendar; or an AdwPreferencesGroup per account with a header suffix widget. Inline edit/remove ToolButtons → flat Gtk.Buttons in the row suffix. Empty states (PlaceholderMessage) → AdwStatusPage (with icon, title, description, and an optional action button). FormSectionText hints → AdwPreferencesGroup description or a dim Gtk.Label. Add/Edit Kirigami.Dialog with a form + custom footer actions → AdwDialog (or AdwPreferencesDialog subpage) containing AdwPreferencesGroup rows and header/footer Gtk.Buttons; the remove PromptDialog → AdwAlertDialog with destructive-action styling on the Remove button. Toasts (showPassiveNotification) → AdwToast via an AdwToastOverlay wrapping the window. FileDialog for restore → Gtk.FileDialog (async open). Page actions ('Add', 'Sync now', 'Sync all now') → AdwHeaderBar buttons (start/end) — do not float them. The 'auto-discover' / config-changed live-apply banners could use AdwBanner if a restart hint were ever needed (not here — applies live). Charts are not present in this slice. The Loader-per-type dispatch (bool/enum/quicklaunch/number/color) → a small factory in code that returns the appropriate Adw*Row per pref type; the QML page-scope precompute of display data (qlOptions, colorPresetList) maps naturally to preparing model objects before building rows.
gotchas: 'notifications' is filtered out of the Sync services list (lives on the Notifications tab); dnd is present and labelled 'Do Not Disturb'
After ANY mutating call the page re-fetches its own list (getSyncStatus/refreshCalendars/listWatchPrefs/getConfig) — the signal is only a best-effort poke, the re-fetch is authoritative
Result parsing lives in StoandlClient, never QML: rows expose {ok,kind,tail,fields[],values{}}; QML only reads them. kind:message is split on first ':'

result.purpose: StoandlClient is the ONE object that touches D-Bus; registered as a QML singleton (QML_ELEMENT + QML_SINGLETON, module org.stoandl.gui). Three jobs: call the daemon, parse every reply, and poll as a safety net. All QML pages call its Q_INVOKABLE methods; QML never builds D-Bus messages, never parses, never polls. It talks to de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control on the SESSION bus, path /de/yoxcu/stoandl, and augments 7 reactive daemon signals with polling fallbacks because the daemon is NOT D-Bus-activated (a late/reconnecting client can miss a signal).
features: Session-bus connection built once in the constructor (QDBusConnection::sessionBus()). Constants: SERVICE=de.yoxcu.stoandl, PATH=/de/yoxcu/stoandl, IFACE=de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control.
Two Q_PROPERTYs to QML: daemonUp (bool, NOTIFY daemonUpChanged) and bluetoothOn (bool, NOTIFY bluetoothOnChanged; defaults true until first BluetoothStatus poll says otherwise).

Daemon liveness: recheckDaemon() calls org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner(SERVICE) (3s timeout) at construction and before every refresh*; onNameOwnerChanged reacts to NameOwnerChanged to flip daemonUp without polling.
startDaemon(): QProcess::startDetached systemctl --user start stoandl, then two fallback recheckDaemon() at 1.5s and 4s.
Generic escape hatches: call(method,args)->{kind,tail,fields[],ok,notready}; list(method,args)->[[f0,f1,...]] (tab-split records).

Status parsing: parseStatus splits reply on FIRST ':' only (kind:tail; tail may contain colons); tail then tab-split into fields[]. statusMap adds ok(kind=='ok') and notready(kind=='notready') booleans.

Low-level calls hand-built via QDBusMessage::createMethodCall (NO QDBusInterface, to avoid introspection blocking on a missing daemon). Blocking calls: CALL_TIMEOUT_MS=10000 ordinary, FIND_TIMEOUT_MS=20000 for FindWatch, NAME_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 for NameHasOwner.

Error handling: a D-Bus ErrorMessage becomes {kind:'error', tail:errorMessage}; daemon-reported error/failed/timeout kinds also logged to stderr (Q_LOGGING_CATEGORY 'stoandl', QtWarningMsg; tune via QT_LOGGING_RULES).

result.component: D-Bus interface contract — the full `de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control` surface (51 original methods + drift-report hooks, 7 signals, status kinds). Covered files: /workspace/docs/handoff/dbus-interface.md, /workspace/docs/handoff/drift-report.md. This is the authoritative method inventory the new GTK4/libadwaita client must speak.
result.purpose: Defines the single control interface (session bus, name `de.yoxcu.stoandl`, path `/de/yoxcu/stoandl`, interface `de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control`) that every stoandl front-end (CLI, current Kirigami GUI, the planned GTK4 rewrite) speaks to. It is the only contract between the daemon and any out-of-process client; no code is shared, the client is purely a D-Bus consumer plus a shell-out to the co-located `stoandl` CLI for the three non-D-Bus operations (backup/restore/support).
features: Bus identity: session bus, bus name `de.yoxcu.stoandl`, object path `/de/yoxcu/stoandl`, interface `de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control`. 51 original methods + drift-report hook methods, 7 signals, 0 properties.

NOT D-Bus-activated: the daemon calls requestBusName at startup and releaseBusName on shutdown (systemd user service `packaging/stoandl.service`, also OpenRC). A client that finds the bus name unowned must itself start/enable the service (systemctl --user start stoandl) — never assume it is up.

Only 4 D-Bus type signatures across all methods: `s` (String), `b` (Boolean), `as` (List<String>, one record per row, fields tab-separated), and empty/void (only WebviewClose). No numeric/struct/dict/variant/object-path types on the control interface.

Status-string convention: most methods return a single String shaped `kind:message` — a status token, first colon, then a human/payload tail. Split on the FIRST colon only. Multi-field payloads are tab-separated in the tail (e.g. `ok:<name>\t<level>`).

Watch group methods: ListWatches()→as, Battery()→s, Connect(s)→s, Pair()→s, PairStatus()→s, Repair(s)→s, Unpair(s)→s (empty=all, name=single, exact-then-substring), FindWatch()→b (rings the watch; false=not ready).

Apps/faces group: ListApps()→as, LaunchApp(s)→s (by uuid or name; also the set-active-face mechanism — NO dedicated SetActiveFace), RemoveApp(s)→s (system apps refused), SideloadApp(s)→s (local .pbw, absolute daemon-side path), OpenConfig(s)→s (Clay/PKJS config URL or empty), WebviewClose(s)→void (hand settings JSON back to running PKJS app).

Watch-prefs group: ListWatchPrefs()→as (~46 prefs), SetWatchPref(s,s)→s. Pref record: id/type/current/default/allowed/flags/name/description; flags carries `debug` for advanced prefs; `allowed` is PIPE-separated for enum/quicklaunch/color.

No SyncMusic/SyncNotifications, no per-service master toggle in the original 51.

Firmware group: CheckFirmware()→s (`ok:board\tcurrent\tlatest\tasset\tyes|no\tsource\tchangelogUrl` — changelogUrl is the new 7th field, or noasset:/disabled:/notready:/error:), UpdateFirmware()→s, SideloadFirmware(s path)→s (local .pbz, absolute daemon-side path), FirmwareStatus()→s (polled: idle:/downloading:<asset>/waiting:/inprogress:<percent>/reboot:/failed:<reason>/notready:).

JSON in the status tail — the only place this contract uses JSON; parse in the shim, not the UI.

Empty value field = no-data point (hasValue=false).
