DROPPED hooks the new client must NOT call: NotifGetQuietHours/NotifSetQuietHours/NotifSetQuietNow (superseded by dnd.sync), and Repair/PairStatus dropped from the UI (plumbing stays in shim but no re-pair affordance).
result.uiStructure: This slice is the D-Bus contract, not a UI page — it has no widgets of its own. It is the data/RPC layer consumed by all five GTK4 pages. The contract dictates: (1) all list data arrives as `as` (arrays of tab-separated string records) that a client-side shim must parse into typed row models; (2) all mutating calls return `kind:message` status strings that must be split on the first colon and mapped to UI states/toasts; (3) 7 signals form a reactive push layer that must AUGMENT (never replace) a slow safety-net poll and a re-sync on daemon-up; (4) three operations (Pair, Firmware flash, Language install) are long-running and surfaced as POLLED status strings with the progress signals only smoothing the % between watchdog ticks. Long-running op cadences/timeouts/terminal states: Pair/Repair via PairStatus() at 1.5s / 145s timeout / terminal ok:|error:|timeout: (pending:<msg> continues); Firmware flash via FirmwareStatus() at 0.8s / 600s / terminal reboot: or post-activity notready: = success, failed: = failure; Language install via LanguageStatus() at 0.6s (relaxed to 3s watchdog with the signal) / 180s / terminal done: = success, failed: = failure, post-activity notready: = disconnected. Record field layouts: ListWatches = name·state(connected|connecting|disconnected)·battery(0-100 or empty)·transport(ble|classic, empty when disconnected); ListApps = uuid·type·order·flags(⊆active,sideloaded,config,system,synced)·title·developer·version; ListWatchPrefs = id·type·current·default·allowed·flags·name·description; ListCalendars = id·name·enabled|disabled·accountId; ListCalendarSources = id·type(caldav|ical|ics)·url·username·label (never password); ListLanguages = id·isoLocal·displayName·installed(yes|no)·source(rebble|github); NotifList = name·muteLabel·color·icon·vibe·lastNotifiedEpochSeconds; ExtList = name·installed|missing·enabled|disabled·running|stopped·config·description·author·version; GetSyncStatus = service·enabled·available·lastSync; NotifListFilters = pattern·action(allow|block).
dbusOrClientCalls: Version() → s: daemon version string; soft — client should fall back to its own embedded version if the daemon is down.
ListWatches() → as: known watches, one record `name\tstate\tbattery\ttransport`. Primary Watch-list data source; also the missed-WatchesChanged safety net (poll ~20s).
Battery() → s: active watch battery `ok:<name>\t<level>` / `unknown:<name>` / `notready:`.
Connect(s name) → s: connect/switch to a known watch by name (exact-then-unique-substring).
Pair() → s: open ~2-min pairing window, returns ok: immediately, then poll PairStatus.
PairStatus() → s: pairing outcome pending:<msg> / ok: / error: / timeout:. (UI dropped re-pair; plumbing retained.)
Repair(s name) → s: forget one watch + reopen pairing window; poll PairStatus. (UI-dropped, shim-retained.)
Unpair(s name) → s: forget watch(es); empty=all, name=single (exact-then-substring).
FindWatch() → b: ring the watch continuously until a button is pressed; false = not ready.
ListApps() → as: locker (apps+faces), record `uuid\ttype\torder\tflags\ttitle\tdeveloper\tversion`; flags ⊆ {active,sideloaded,config,system,synced}.
LaunchApp(s name|uuid) → s: launch app/face; on a face this ALSO sets it active (no SetActiveFace). ok:/notfound:/ambiguous:/notready:/error:. After call re-read ListApps — the active flag moves.
RemoveApp(s name|uuid) → s: uninstall from locker (system apps refused).
SideloadApp(s path) → s: install a local .pbw at an absolute daemon-side path.
OpenConfig(s app) → s: Clay/PKJS config URL for a running app, empty string if none.
WebviewClose(s json) → void: hand saved settings JSON back to the running PKJS app after the config webview closes. The only void method.
ListWatchPrefs() → as: ~46 watch prefs, record `id\ttype\tcurrent\tdefault\tallowed\tflags\tname\tdescription`; allowed is PIPE-separated for enum/quicklaunch/color; flags carries `debug`.
SetWatchPref(s id, s value) → s: set a pref, value parsed per the pref's type.
NotifList() → as: per-app notif store, record `name\tmuteLabel\tcolor\ticon\tvibe\tlastNotifiedEpochSeconds`; muteLabel ∈ never/always/weekdays/weekends or `muted-until <instant>`.
NotifSetMute(s query, s spec) → s: set per-app mute; spec always/never/weekdays/weekends or duration; unmute sends `never`.
NotifSetMuteAll(s spec) → s: apply spec to every tracked app; NO getter — master snooze must be derived from NotifList.
NotifSetStyle(s query, s color, s icon, s vibe) → s: per-app styling; empty=unchanged, `default`=reset.
NotifListFilters() → as: regex filters `pattern\taction` (allow|block).
NotifAddFilter(s pattern, s action) → s: add a regex filter.
NotifRemoveFilter(s pattern) → s: remove a filter by pattern.
SyncWeather() → s: fetch weather now and push; error: if weather not enabled.
SyncCalendar() → s: re-read calendar sources → timeline pins; error: if calendar not enabled.
SyncHealth() → s: request fresh health/activity + re-project export; error: if not enabled (there is NO disabled: kind here).
ListCalendars() → as: synced calendars `id\tname\tenabled|disabled\taccountId` (accountId groups under source).
SetCalendarEnabled(s id|name, b enabled) → s: toggle one calendar.
ListCalendarSources() → as: editable sources `id\ttype\turl\tusername\tlabel`; type∈caldav|ical|ics; never the password.
AddCalendarSource(s type, s url, s username, s password) → s: add source; ok:<id>\t<backend> / error:. Live, no restart.
UpdateCalendarSource(s id, s url, s username, s password) → s: edit by id; blank password KEEPS stored; ok:<id>\t<backend|kept|none> / notfound: / error:.
RemoveCalendarSource(s id) → s: remove by id + stored password; ok:removed / notfound: / error:.
GetSyncStatus() → as: `service\tenabled\tavailable\tlastSync` for notifications/weather/calendar/music/health/dnd — initializes the sync toggles + last-sync labels.
SetSyncEnabled(s service, b enabled) → s: runtime master on/off per service.
CheckFirmware() → s: ok:<board>\t<current>\t<latest>\t<asset>\t<yes|no>\t<source>\t<changelogUrl> / noasset:/disabled:/notready:/error:.
UpdateFirmware() → s: download newer fw + start flashing; ok:<board>\t<current>\t<latest>\t<asset> / uptodate:/noasset:/busy:/disabled:/notready:/error:; then poll FirmwareStatus.
SideloadFirmware(s path) → s: flash a local .pbz (absolute daemon-side path), async; poll FirmwareStatus.
FirmwareStatus() → s: idle:/downloading:<asset>/waiting:/inprogress:<percent>/reboot:(success)/failed:<reason>/notready:.
ListLanguages() → as: catalog packs `id\tisoLocal\tdisplayName\tinstalled(yes|no)\tsource(rebble|github)`; soft — falls back to offline bundled catalog.
InstallLanguage(s locale|name|id) → s: auto-pick + download + install (blank=system locale); ok:<displayName> / notfound:/disabled:/notready:/error:; poll LanguageStatus.
SideloadLanguage(s path) → s: install a local .pbl (absolute daemon-side path), async; poll LanguageStatus.
LanguageStatus() → s: idle:/downloading:<name>/installing:<percent>/done:<name>/failed:<reason>/notready:.
TakeScreenshot(s path) → s: capture PNG to absolute daemon-side path; ok:<path>\t<w>\t<h> / notready:/error:; blocks seconds.
GatherLogs(s path) → s: dump watch fw logs to a text file; ok:<path> / notready:/error:; blocks seconds.
GetCoreDump(s path) → s: fetch existing coredump; ok:<path> / none: / notready:/error:.
WatchInfoText() → s: watch metadata as an inline human-readable text block; ok:<text> / notready:. Returned inline (no file).
ResetIntoRecovery() → s: reboot the watch into recovery (PRF); fire-and-forget (ok:=queued).
FactoryReset() → s: wipe watch to out-of-box + reboot; destructive, fire-and-forget; client owns confirmation.
StartDevConnection() → s: start LAN WebSocket server; ok:9000 (binds 0.0.0.0, NO AUTH) / notready:/error:.
StopDevConnection() → s: stop the developer server.
DevConnectionStatus() → s: ok:active / ok:inactive / notready: — seeds the dev toggle's initial value.
ExtList() → as: extensions `name\tinstalled|missing\tenabled|disabled\trunning|stopped\tconfig\tdescription\tauthor\tversion`; config∈none|url|schema.
ExtInstall(s archive) → s: install from .tar.gz/.tgz/.tar/.zip (absolute daemon-side path): extract, sideload .pbw, enable, hotplug-start.
ExtUninstall(s name, b keepConfig) → s: stop, drop from extensions.enabled, delete files; keepConfig retains config file.
ExtEnable(s name) → s: add to extensions.enabled + hotplug-start.
ExtDisable(s name) → s: remove from extensions.enabled + stop (files kept).
ExtRestart(s name) → s: restart the extension process (also un-quarantines).
ExtOpenConfig(s name) → s: ok:<http-url> (url backend) / none: / error: (schema backend).
ExtConfigSchema(s name) → s: ok:<json-array> of {key,type,label,secret?,options?}; types bool/string(+secret)/int/enum(+options).
ExtGetConfig(s name) → s: ok:<json-object> of current values.
ExtSetConfig(s name, s json) → s: save the JSON values.
GetHealthSummary() → s: ok: + 21 tab fields (today totals, week avgs, trends, sleep light/deep, bedtime/wakeup/typical, resting/current HR, hrMin/hrMax, hrAvailable, lastSync).
GetHealthSeries(s metric) → as: steps/heart → label\tvalue; sleep → last night's startFraction\twidthFraction\tisDeep; heart → [] when HR unavailable; empty value field = no-data point.
GetConfigSchema() → as: `key\ttype\tlabel\toptions\tdesc` for curated stoandl.conf keys.
GetConfig() → as: `key\tvalue`.
SetConfig(s key, s value) → s: set one config key.
WatchDetails() → s: ok:name\tcode\tmodel\tplatform\ttransport\tfirmware\tserial\tbattery\tlastSync / notready: (Board omitted).
BluetoothStatus() → s: ok:on / ok:off (host BT usability; catches rfkill/airplane-mode). Poll on the 20s watch tick.
SetWatchNickname(s watch, s nickname) → s: rename a known watch.
GetAppIcon(s uuid) → s: ok:<abs png path> / none:/notready:/error: — lazy per-row app/face menu icon, cached at <configDir>/icons/<uuid>.png.
FakeCallRing(s name, s number) → b: inject a synthetic ringing call; false=not ready.
FakeCallEnd() → b: clear the current synthetic call.
SIGNAL WatchesChanged() → poke, re-call ListWatches (connect/disconnect/pair-completion).
SIGNAL FirmwareProgress(s phase, i percent, s detail) → push flash progress; phase vocabulary = FirmwareStatus; percent 0-100 while inprogress else -1; detail=asset/reason.
SIGNAL LockerChanged() → poke, re-call ListApps (install/remove + active-watchface change).
SIGNAL LanguageProgress(s phase, i percent, s detail) → push language-install progress; phase vocabulary = LanguageStatus; percent 0-100 while installing else -1.
SIGNAL ExtensionsChanged() → poke, re-call ExtList (enable/disable/restart/install/uninstall, incl. CLI/other-client).

SIGNAL ExtensionStateChanged(s name, s state) → per-extension run-state transition; state∈ready|exited|quarantined; overrides the stale polled running (a quarantined ext stays in the daemon's running map).
SIGNAL CalendarsChanged() → poke, re-call ListCalendars (+ListCalendarSources) when an async sync adds/drops calendars after a source CRUD.

NON-D-BUS (shell out to co-located `stoandl` CLI): backup [out] and restore <in> [--force] (pure CLI-local tar over ~/.config/stoandl — NO Backup/Restore method); support [out.tar.gz] (CLI-local assembly — NO SupportBundle method). Also CLI-local: calendar dump, datalog list|dump|tail, health readers (only health sync hits the daemon), notif styles.
states: Universal status kinds (first token before the colon): ok, error, notready (libPebble not up / no watch — the canonical no-watch empty state), notfound, ambiguous, pending, timeout, disabled, idle, inprogress, reboot, failed, done, uptodate, noasset, busy, none, unknown, plus confirm (PairStatus `confirm:<code>` numeric-compare awaiting ConfirmPairing).
ListWatches state field per watch: connected | connecting | disconnected. Battery empty for non-connected; transport empty when disconnected.

Firmware flash states (FirmwareStatus / FirmwareProgress.phase): idle, downloading, waiting, inprogress, reboot (success), failed, notready. Post-activity notready: after seen activity = success (link dropped on reboot).
Language install states (LanguageStatus / LanguageProgress.phase): idle, downloading, installing, done (success), failed, notready. First-poll stale sticky done:/idle:/failed: is skipped once.

Extension run-state (ExtensionStateChanged): ready (handshake done/running), exited (process ended, restarting after backoff), quarantined (gave up after rapid failures — won't restart until ExtRestart). ExtList polled run field is only running|stopped, so a quarantined ext still shows running unless overridden by the signal.

Three top-level client states: daemon-down (bus name unowned → hide nav, offer systemctl --user start stoandl), no-watch (notready → placeholder/status page), and Bluetooth-off (BluetoothStatus ok:off — daemon up but BT unusable, a distinct third state).
Sync service state (GetSyncStatus): enabled, available, lastSync per service (notifications/weather/calendar/music/health/dnd).
Health HR availability: hrAvailable flag in GetHealthSummary + GetHealthSeries('heart') returning [] — hide the HR card when absent, never fabricate.
Reset ops have no completion state: ok: = queued only, no ack, link drops.
GetHealthSeries no-data point: empty value field → hasValue=false (e.g. a future weekday).
interactions: No direct user interactions in this slice — it is the RPC layer. The interactions it ENABLES map to the UI pages: watch connect/unpair/find/rename, app launch/install/remove/config, pref edits, notification mute/style/filter, calendar source CRUD + per-calendar toggle, sync master toggles + force-sync, firmware check/update/sideload, language install/sideload, screenshot/logs/coredump/info, reset recovery/factory, dev-connection start/stop, extension enable/disable/restart/install/uninstall + config.
Contract-level rule the client must honor: after ANY mutating call, still re-fetch that screen's list — the signal is a best-effort poke, the re-fetch is authoritative.
Long-running ops (Pair, Firmware flash, Language install) require the client to start-then-poll with the documented cadences/timeouts and treat post-activity notready: as success.
Destructive FactoryReset and the forget/unpair actions require the CLIENT to own the confirmation dialog (daemon does not confirm).
signalsConsumed: WatchesChanged() — re-call ListWatches (also a 20s safety-net poll carries BluetoothStatus and catches missed pokes).
FirmwareProgress(s phase, i percent, s detail) — smooth flash % between FirmwareStatus watchdog ticks.
LockerChanged() — re-call ListApps.
LanguageProgress(s phase, i percent, s detail) — smooth install % (op-poll relaxed to 3s watchdog).
ExtensionsChanged() — re-call ExtList.
ExtensionStateChanged(s name, s state) — record in a name→state map, merge into ExtList rows, override the stale polled running.
CalendarsChanged() — re-call ListCalendars (+ListCalendarSources); page also keeps a short post-mutation settle-timer fallback.

Fallbacks the client must ALSO keep because the daemon isn't D-Bus-activated: a slow safety-net poll (20s watch tick), re-sync on daemon-up (bus-name-owned transition), and op-pollers for Pair/Firmware/Language as the reboot/disconnect watchdog.
No PropertiesChanged / org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties — the interface has 0 properties; watch org.freedesktop.DBus NameOwnerChanged for daemon up/down.
result.gnomeMappingNotes: This slice is non-visual, so the mapping is about the client-side D-Bus plumbing rather than widgets. Kirigami's C++ StoandlClient shim → a GObject service class (e.g. StoandlClient) built on Gio.DBusProxy for `de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control` on the session bus, exposing typed GObject properties + signals so GTK templates bind reactively; connect proxy 'g-signal' to demux the 7 custom signals. Bus-name presence → Gio.bus_watch_name (NameOwnerChanged) to drive daemon-up/down; when down, show an AdwStatusPage with a 'Start service' button that runs systemctl --user start stoandl. `as` tab-separated records → parse in the shim into GObject row structs backing Gtk/Gio.ListStore + Gtk.ColumnView/Gtk.ListView (never parse in the .ui). `kind:message` status → map to AdwToast (transient results) via AdwToastOverlay, AdwBanner (persistent e.g. 'Bluetooth off', firmware 'What's new' with changelogUrl link), and AdwAlertDialog for destructive confirms (FactoryReset, unpair/forget). Long-running polled ops → a GLib timeout_add poll loop feeding a Gtk.ProgressBar / AdwActionRow subtitle, with FirmwareProgress/LanguageProgress signals updating the fraction between ticks. notready/no-watch/daemon-down/BT-off → four AdwStatusPage variants. Health series → Gtk.DrawingArea (Cairo) for step/HR/sleep charts. Extension/config JSON schema (ExtConfigSchema) → dynamically built AdwPreferencesGroup with AdwSwitchRow/AdwEntryRow(+password for secret)/AdwSpinRow/AdwComboRow per field type. Enum/quicklaunch/color WatchPrefs (allowed is pipe-separated) → AdwComboRow; number prefs → AdwSpinRow with a debounced write; bool → AdwSwitchRow; color → a custom swatch row (avoid any i18ndc-calling helper). App/face icons via GetAppIcon path → Gtk.Image/Gdk.Texture loaded lazily per row. Since there are 0 D-Bus properties and only pokes, the client keeps its own GObject 'properties' as the reactive source of truth and refreshes them from method re-fetches on each signal.
gotchas: Split status strings on the FIRST colon only — the tail can itself contain colons (URLs, instants, error messages).
Tab is the field separator within both `as` records AND multi-field `kind:message` tails — never split payloads on colon beyond the first.

`allowed` in ListWatchPrefs is PIPE(|)-separated for enum/quicklaunch/color, NOT comma. Enum options are DISPLAY names, not Kotlin constant names. Quicklaunch options are app names (from ListApps) + 'Off', never a slider/uuid.
Number-pref `current` may carry a unit (e.g. '3000 ms') — take the leading digits, not a plain int parse.
The daemon is NOT D-Bus-activated: a late/reconnecting client can miss any of the 7 signals, so polling + daemon-up re-sync must remain as the fallback; signals only augment.
After every mutating call, re-fetch the list authoritatively — the signal poke is best-effort.
notready is the canonical 'no watch / libPebble not up' empty state and appears across almost every method — handle it uniformly.
SyncWeather/SyncCalendar/SyncHealth signal 'service disabled' via `error:` (not a `disabled:` kind) — a dead disabled-branch bug was found and removed for Health sync.
NotifSetMuteAll has NO getter — the master mute/snooze state is write-only and must be DERIVED from the per-app NotifList.

ExtList's polled run field is only running|stopped; a quarantined/crashed ext still shows 'running' (daemon keeps it in its running map) unless the client overrides it with ExtensionStateChanged (ready|exited|quarantined).
CheckFirmware gained a 7th field changelogUrl; the fw success flag is field 5 (yes|no). Update parsers for the extra field.

Firmware/Language: a successful op ends with the watch rebooting so the link drops — treat post-activity notready: (after having seen activity) as SUCCESS, not failure. Language install skips one stale sticky terminal value on the first poll.
Reset (recovery/factory) is fire-and-forget: ok: means queued, there is no completion ack; rely on the connection-state drop/reconnect for confirmation.

Screenshot/logs/coredump return DAEMON-SIDE absolute file paths — fine only because the GUI is co-located; a remote/sandboxed client would need the deferred byte-returning variants (not implemented). WatchInfoText is the exception (inline text).
All sideload/install path args (SideloadApp/SideloadFirmware/SideloadLanguage/ExtInstall/TakeScreenshot/GatherLogs/GetCoreDump) are ABSOLUTE DAEMON-SIDE paths.
ExtConfigSchema/ExtGetConfig carry JSON in the status tail — the ONLY place this contract uses JSON; parse in the shim. Field types: bool/string(+secret)/int/enum(+options).

GetHealthSeries uses an EMPTY value field to mark a no-data point (hasValue=false), e.g. a future weekday; GetHealthSeries('heart') returns [] and hrAvailable gates the HR card — never fabricate HR data.
WatchDetails omits Board (per drift-report §4d) even though WatchInfoText's free text includes board — don't expect a board field in WatchDetails.
Quiet-hours hooks (NotifGetQuietHours/SetQuietHours/SetQuietNow) were DROPPED (superseded by dnd.sync) — do not call them. Repair/PairStatus are shim-retained but the UI dropped re-pair.
StartDevConnection binds 0.0.0.0 with NO AUTH on port 9000 — surface this as a security caveat in the UI.

There are 0 properties on the interface — no PropertiesChanged; watches battery changes are NOT pushed (learned only by calling Battery/ListWatches again). The 7 signals are the entire reactive surface.

WatchDetails/BluetoothStatus/SetWatchNickname/GetSyncStatus/SetSyncEnabled/Ext*Config/GetHealth*/Get|SetConfig/GetAppIcon/CheckFirmware-changelog are drift-report HOOKS implemented in the mock (tools/mock_stoandl.py) and MUST be grown in the real Kotlin daemon to match — a client hitting an un-updated daemon will get method-not-found for these.

result.component: Build + test + packaging infra: mock daemon (tools/mock_stoandl.py), run harness (tools/run-with-mock.sh), CMake build (CMakeLists.txt), app-id / desktop entry / AppStream metainfo / icon theme (data/*), and the headless verification approach.
result.purpose: This slice is the developer/packaging scaffolding, not user-facing UI. It lets the app be built out-of-tree, exercised headlessly against a stateful stand-in for the (JVM+BLE) stoandl daemon on an ephemeral session bus, and installed as a proper desktop application (launcher entry, AppStream metainfo, hicolor icon theme). For the GTK4 rewrite it defines the exact D-Bus contract to test against, the app id / desktop-file / icon naming that must be preserved, and the smoke-test methodology.
features: Mock daemon (tools/mock_stoandl.py) — a single Python3 class MockStoandl(dbus.service.Object) claiming well-known name de.yoxcu.stoandl, object path /de/yoxcu/stoandl, interface de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control on the SESSION bus; run via `dbus-run-session -- python3 mock_stoandl.py`.

The mock is STATEFUL: mutating calls update in-memory state; long-running ops (Pair/Firmware/Language) walk pending->terminal across polls so both the poll loops and the re-fetch-after-mutation path light up.

Return-value contract mirrored exactly: statuses are `kind:tail` (split on first colon); list methods return `as` (array of strings), each a TAB-joined record via helper rec(*fields). Status kinds used: ok, error, notready, notfound, ambiguous, pending, timeout, inprogress, reboot, done, idle, none, confirm.
Implements the ~51 documented Control methods the GUI touches PLUS the milestone daemon-side hooks (flagged HOOK #n inline) — the new D-Bus contract the real Kotlin daemon must grow to match.

Emits all seven reactive signals so the push-on-top-of-polling path is exercised: WatchesChanged(), FirmwareProgress(s,i,s), LockerChanged(), LanguageProgress(s,i,s), ExtensionsChanged(), ExtensionStateChanged(s,s), CalendarsChanged() (note: CalendarsChanged is referenced in CLAUDE.md but the mock file's signal block defines only the first six — the rest are present).

Firmware/language progress walkers driven by GLib.timeout_add (~700ms cadence) push *Progress signals step-by-step (fw: downloading->waiting->inprogress 20/40/60/80/100->reboot + WatchesChanged; lang: downloading->installing 25/50/75/100->done) while FirmwareStatus/LanguageStatus give a NON-advancing polled snapshot of the same walk (so signal and poll never double-advance).

Pairing state machine: Pair()/Repair() open a window; PairStatus() walks search(pending)->confirm:<code=481516>->(parks until ConfirmPairing(bool))->done->registers+connects a new watch; Repair restores the popped watch's info.

Extension crash simulation ExtCrash (MOCK-ONLY, not in real contract): fires ExtensionStateChanged(name,'exited') immediately then 'quarantined' on an 800ms GLib one-shot, while polled ExtList keeps the ext 'running' — proving only the signal reveals quarantine.

GetAppIcon writes a real 25x25 RGBA PNG per app to $TMPDIR/stoandl-mock-icons/<uuid>.png using pure stdlib zlib/struct (no Pillow), tinted from a uuid hash; system apps + Isotime return `none:` to exercise the generic-icon fallback branch.

Health data is generated DETERMINISTICALLY from each date's ordinal (steps/sleep/heart/typicals), so GetHealthSummary(periodType,offset) (20 fields) and GetHealthSeries(metric,periodType,offset) all return realistic day/week/month data with gaps (~1/11 ordinals absent) and sparse HR days (~1/13).
Diagnostic methods actually write files to the caller-supplied absolute path (TakeScreenshot writes a 1x1 base64 PNG; GatherLogs, GetCoreDump write stub content) and return ok:<path>.

run-with-mock.sh: launches the GUI on a fresh ephemeral session bus with the mock; three modes — default (run GUI), QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen prefix (headless smoke test), and --mock-only (just the mock, Ctrl-C to stop).

The harness spawns the mock, waits up to 5s (50 x 0.1s) for it to claim the bus name (checked via dbus.SessionBus().name_has_owner), then exec's the GUI; a trap kills the mock on EXIT so the whole thing lives and dies with one process. GUI binary is overridable via $GUI env (default $ROOT/build/stoandl-gui); errors if not executable.

CMake build: Qt6>=6.5 only (Core Gui Widgets Qml Quick QuickControls2 DBus); Kirigami + KirigamiAddons are pure-QML RUNTIME modules and deliberately NOT find_package'd/linked. C++17, AUTOMOC. Single C++ shim StoandlClient + main.cpp; QML registered via qt_add_qml_module URI org.stoandl.gui.

App icon PNGs (16..256) embedded as a Qt resource (qt_add_resources PREFIX /icons, aliases :/icons/<size>/apps/...) so the window icon shows uninstalled from build/; installed hicolor theme icon preferred at runtime via QIcon::fromTheme.
Install rules: binary to bindir; .desktop to <datadir>/applications; metainfo.xml to <datadir>/metainfo; icons/hicolor tree to <datadir>/icons (PNG+SVG).

Application ID de.yoxcu.stoandl.gui is shared across: desktop-file basename, Wayland app_id (setDesktopFileName in main.cpp), Icon= key, metainfo <id>, and QIcon theme name — reverse-DNS of setOrganizationDomain yoxcu.de, sibling of daemon bus name de.yoxcu.stoandl.
Icon theme is the single source of truth in data/icons/hicolor: scalable SVG + -symbolic SVG + raster fallbacks 16..512px (a two-arrow refresh/sync mark, teal #0f9d94, symbolic ink #232629).

result.gnomeMappingNotes: The mock daemon, run harness, and D-Bus contract are TOOLKIT-AGNOSTIC and carry over verbatim: the GTK4 app is just another de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control client on the session bus, so keep tools/mock_stoandl.py and run-with-mock.sh as-is (only $GUI points at the new binary). Use Gio.DBusProxy / Gio.DBusConnection.call (or a generated codegen client) in the GTK app; subscribe to the six/seven signals via g_dbus_connection_signal_subscribe; check the bus name with Gio.bus_watch_name / DBusProxy g-name-owner (equivalent of NameHasOwner + NameOwnerChanged). Parse the `kind:tail` and TAB-record returns in one client shim (analog of StoandlClient), never in UI code. Build system: replace CMake+Qt with Meson + gnome.compile_resources (GResource for UI XML + icons) + desktop_file/appstream validation (meson's install_data + `desktop-file-validate` and `appstreamcli validate` test hooks). Keep the same install layout: bindir binary, <datadir>/applications/<appid>.desktop, <datadir>/metainfo/<appid>.metainfo.xml, <datadir>/icons/hicolor/**. App id de.yoxcu.stoandl.gui stays identical and becomes the GApplication application-id, the Wayland app_id, the .desktop basename, and the GResource base path (/de/yoxcu/stoandl/gui). desktop-file X-KDE/X-Purism form-factor keys drop; GTK convergence is via AdwBreakpoint, not desktop-file hints. The .metainfo.xml is already freedesktop-standard (works for GNOME Software unchanged; consider adding <recommends><control>touch/pointer/keyboard</control> and screenshots). Icons: keep the hicolor tree; GNOME strongly prefers a full-color scalable SVG + a -symbolic SVG (both already present) — no need to embed PNGs in a resource since GTK loads themed icons via Gtk.IconTheme (the Qt-resource-embedding workaround for the uninstalled Wayland case is unnecessary). Headless verification maps to: run the GTK app under `dbus-run-session` with the mock; there is no offscreen-QPA equivalent, but you can smoke-test by launching with GDK_BACKEND set and driving the AdwViewStack pages, or use `broadway`/headless Wayland (wlheadless-run / a nested compositor) for screenshots — GTK does rasterize offscreen better than Qt's offscreen QPA, so grab-to-file via a GskRenderer render_node or `gnome-screenshot` under a nested compositor is feasible.

gotchas: `allowed` field for enum/quicklaunch/color/number prefs is PIPE (|)-separated, NOT comma — parse on '|'. (App flags and config-schema options ARE comma-separated — don't confuse them.)

Enum current/allowed use DISPLAY names, not Kotlin constant names. Number current/default carry the unit inline ('3000 ms') — use leading digits for the int. quicklaunch current is an app name / 'off' / a raw uuid.

SetWatchPref round-trips the value: color -> resolves a preset NAME (via COLOR_PRESETS, lowercased) first then a hex to 0xRRGGBB; number -> re-appends the unit parsed from allowed; quicklaunch ''/off/none/disabled -> 'off'. The read-back after a mutation differs from what was sent.

Signal is a best-effort POKE, not authoritative — after every mutating call the GUI must STILL re-fetch that screen's list. The daemon is NOT D-Bus-activated, so a late/reconnecting client can miss a signal; polling is the guaranteed fallback and the app re-syncs on daemonUpChanged.

ExtCrash proves the crux of ExtensionStateChanged: polled ExtList keeps the ext 'running' the whole time; only the signal reveals exited->quarantined. The client must record name->state and override the stale polled 'running'.

FirmwareStatus/LanguageStatus are NON-advancing snapshots; the GLib walker owns the step counter and pushes the *Progress signals — so polling and the signal must not both advance the walk (the signal just smooths the % between poll ticks).
run-with-mock.sh waits up to 5s (50x0.1s, checking name_has_owner) for the mock to own the bus name before exec'ing the GUI — race-avoidance; if you swap in a slower mock it may need more retries.

The mock's signal-definition block defines six signals (WatchesChanged, FirmwareProgress, LockerChanged, LanguageProgress, ExtensionsChanged, ExtensionStateChanged) — CalendarsChanged is described in CLAUDE.md/drift-report as the seventh but is not in this file's @dbus.service.signal block; the rewrite's contract should include all seven and the mock may need it added.

Health per-day data is deterministic from date.toordinal(), so tests are stable across runs but shift by real calendar date; ~1/11 ordinals are fully absent and ~1/13 HR days are sparse — assertions must tolerate gaps. GetHealthSummary returns exactly 20 tab fields; day vs week/month change which fields are populated (bedtime/wakeup/hrMin/hrMax/hrCurrent are 0 for week/month).
GetAppIcon returns none: for system apps + Isotime (uuid 3af56a2b) to force the generic-icon branch; real PNGs land in $TMPDIR/stoandl-mock-icons and are cached (written once).

AddCalendarSource/UpdateCalendarSource return a SECOND tab field (backend: keyring|kept|none) after the id — the password is write-only and NEVER returned by ListCalendarSources; blank password on update = keep.

In-container builds MUST go to /tmp/sbuild (or elsewhere outside the mount): /workspace is bind-mounted to the host repo, and a build/ there bakes container paths into CMakeCache.txt and breaks the user's native host build.
qmlcachegen does not fail the build on QML errors (runtime fallback), so `cmake --build` succeeding does NOT mean the QML is valid — always run the offscreen load test.

Screenshots are impossible in this container: no display, no xvfb, and the offscreen QPA doesn't rasterize the scene graph so grabToImage's callback never fires (timers still do). '[QML] Created graphical object was not placed in the graphics scene' warnings during the fast tab-cycle are benign teardown artifacts.

App id (de.yoxcu.stoandl.gui) must stay byte-identical across desktop-file basename, Wayland app_id/setDesktopFileName, Icon= key, metainfo <id>, and QIcon theme name — it's the reverse-DNS of setOrganizationDomain yoxcu.de and a sibling of the daemon bus name de.yoxcu.stoandl. On Wayland the window icon comes from the compositor matching app_id to the INSTALLED .desktop's Icon=; uninstalled from build/ shows no icon (the embedded Qt resource only covers X11/uninstalled).

Grouped rows in labeled FormCard sections separated by FormHeaders. Navigation is Kirigami.NavigationTabBar in the window footer (mobile: below content; desktop: relocates to top). Desktop content is centered and width-constrained (~gridUnit*40 / ~40 grid units max) — FormCards must NOT stretch full-width. Spacing uses the Kirigami unit scale (HIG), never magic px: largeSpacing between groups/cards, smallSpacing within a group, largeSpacing page-edge padding (0 for frameless container views), gridUnit (18px) for fixed sizes, IconSizes.medium for list items with subtitles / IconSizes.smallMedium without. Page title comes free from the page; the only header chrome is the toolbar Kirigami builds from the page `actions`. Dialogs: Kirigami.PromptDialog / bottom-sheet on mobile, popup on desktop. Banners are Kirigami.InlineMessage at top of page. Row actions are INLINE (SwipeListItem pattern: hover buttons with mouse, swipe-to-reveal on touch), not kebabs. Charts are simple SVG (bars + area) themed with Kirigami.Theme colors. Segment/period switchers are pinned in a page header toolbar (not inside scrolling content).
dbusOrClientCalls: Bus contract: session bus, name de.yoxcu.stoandl, path /de/yoxcu/stoandl, iface de.yoxcu.stoandl.Control. Original 51 methods; now augmented with signals + extra hooks.
org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner — detect whether the daemon is running (unowned = down).
Return shapes: status string `kind:message` (split on the FIRST colon) OR `as` array of records with TAB-separated fields. Only s/b/as/void types. Parse in the C++ shim, never in QML.
Status struct { kind, tail, fields[] }; ok() = kind=='ok'. Handle notready as the 'no watch / not ready' empty state.
ListWatches — rows {name,state,battery} (current adds transport). Drives Watch hero + known-watches list; also the focus/watch poll.
Battery — battery for the hero/details.
Connect(name) — connect a known watch.
Pair() then poll PairStatus — pair a new watch; PairStatus kind `confirm:<code>` awaits ConfirmPairing(bool).
Repair(name) / Unpair(name) — re-pair / forget; Unpair("") = forget all.
FindWatch() (b) — Ring watch.
WatchInfoText() / WatchDetails — parsed for the details dialog rows.
TakeScreenshot(absPath) — Capture screenshot.
CheckFirmware — firmware availability + changelogUrl (What's new via xdg-open).
UpdateFirmware() / SideloadFirmware(absPath) then poll FirmwareStatus — flash; success = a `notready` seen AFTER activity (watch reboots, link drops — not an error).
ListLanguages / InstallLanguage(locale) / SideloadLanguage(absPath) then poll LanguageStatus — watch language picker (lives in Watch details).
GatherLogs — Pull watch logs; ResetIntoRecovery — Reboot to recovery/PRF; FactoryReset — Factory reset (red).
ListApps — rows {uuid,type,order,flags,title,developer}; flags ⊆ active,config,system (current adds `synced`). Filter by type for Faces/Apps segments.
LaunchApp(uuid) — tap row to launch (for a face, launch IS set-active).
OpenConfig(app) → URL — Clay/PKJS config; GUI xdg-opens it.
SideloadApp(absPath) — Install .pbw (absolute daemon-side path); re-call ListApps after.
RemoveApp(uuid) — bin action (removes from locker), confirm dialog; re-call ListApps after.
ExtList — rows {name,installed,enabled,config}; config ∈ none|url|schema.
ExtEnable(name)/ExtDisable(name) — the enabled toggle.
ExtOpenConfig(name) → url — Configure via xdg-open (url backend).
ExtConfigSchema(name)/ExtGetConfig(name)/ExtSetConfig(name,json) — native schema form backend (bool→Switch, string→TextField[secret→password], enum→ComboBox, int→SpinBox).
ExtInstall(absArchivePath) — Install extension (.tar.gz/.tgz/.tar/.zip); ExtUninstall(name, keepConfig) — bin with keep-config checkbox; ExtRestart(name). Re-poll ExtList after each.
SyncWeather / SyncCalendar / SyncHealth — force-sync actions.
ListCalendars / SetCalendarEnabled — calendar sources + per-calendar toggles.
GetSyncStatus() → as / SetSyncEnabled(s,b) — per-service master toggles + last-sync labels (hook #5).
GetHealthSummary / GetHealthSeries — health totals + steps/sleep/HR series (hook #8; today only SyncHealth exists).
RenameWatch/SetWatchName — Rename watch (hook #9; may not be feasible).
GetConfigSchema()→as / GetConfig() / SetConfig(key,value) — schema-driven daemon config surface (hook #10).

Seven reactive signals augmenting polling: WatchesChanged, FirmwareProgress(phase,pct,detail), LockerChanged, LanguageProgress(phase,pct,detail), ExtensionsChanged, ExtensionStateChanged(name,state ∈ ready/exited/quarantined), CalendarsChanged. Polling stays as fallback; daemon not D-Bus-activated so a late/reconnecting client can miss a signal.

Polling cadences (fallback): focus poll ListWatches+Battery 4s while a watch screen foreground; list refresh on show + after mutation; Pair 1.5s (≤145s); Firmware 0.8s (≤600s); Language 0.6s→relaxed 3s watchdog (≤180s).
result.gnomeMappingNotes: Top-level nav (5 tabs, Watch launch-first): AdwViewStack + AdwViewSwitcher — switcher in AdwHeaderBar on wide, AdwViewSwitcherBar in the bottom bar on narrow, mapping the Kirigami 'footer on mobile, top on desktop' responsiveness natively. AdwViewSwitcher is window-SIZE driven (a WIN over Kirigami's platform-driven isMobile) — drive off AdwBreakpoint / the switcher's policy, drop any isMobile concept. Each ScrollablePage → AdwNavigationView root page of an AdwToolbarView (AdwHeaderBar top) wrapping a Gtk.ScrolledWindow of AdwPreferencesPage. FormCard groups → AdwPreferencesGroup (FormHeader → group title/description); FormButtonDelegate → AdwActionRow/AdwButtonRow (activatable, trailing icon/chevron); FormSwitchDelegate → AdwSwitchRow; FormComboBoxDelegate → AdwComboRow; FormSpinBoxDelegate → AdwSpinRow; FormTextFieldDelegate → AdwEntryRow / AdwPasswordEntryRow (secret). Extension row (toggle + nested config) → AdwExpanderRow, or an AdwSwitchRow whose activation pushes a config page. Page actions (Kirigami header-desktop/footer-mobile) → primary create/add button in the AdwHeaderBar; GNOME has NO FAB either, so 'no round FAB' carries over — header + button, not a floating circle. Secondary/overflow actions → Gtk.MenuButton + GMenu popover. Watch hero card → activatable AdwActionRow (or custom Gtk.Box in a group) that pushes/opens details. Watch details 'dialog' (bottom sheet mobile / popup desktop) → AdwDialog (auto-adapts: bottom sheet narrow, centered wide) via adw_dialog_present, OR an AdwNavigationPage pushed onto the AdwNavigationView for drill-down (Debug/Language sub-views map to AdwNavigationView.push). Inline hover/swipe row buttons → suffix widgets (flat Gtk.Button) on the AdwActionRow, kept always visible (GTK has no swipe-to-reveal). Firmware/update banner → AdwBanner (top, revealed only when update exists, with a button-label action). Segmented switcher (Faces/Apps/Extensions; Health Daily/Weekly/Monthly) → Gtk.ToggleButton group with 'linked' style class, in the header or a pinned second AdwToolbarView top bar (not scrolling). Radio-list pickers (vibration pattern, language, presets) → AdwComboRow, or a group of check-marked AdwActionRows for a full sub-view. Toasts / passive notifications → AdwToast via an app-wide AdwToastOverlay wrapping window content. Confirm/destructive dialogs → AdwAlertDialog with a .destructive-action response (red). Danger-zone rows (Forget/Factory reset) → AdwButtonRow/AdwActionRow with .destructive-action style, grouped at bottom. Empty/loading/error/daemon-down/notready → AdwStatusPage (icon + title + description + action button, e.g. 'Start the daemon'). Health charts (SVG bars + area) → Gtk.DrawingArea custom draw (or Gtk.Snapshot), colored from libadwaita named/accent colors (never hardcoded); step-goal ring → a DrawingArea arc. Flash/language progress → Gtk.ProgressBar (or banner/row-embedded). Theming: replace Kirigami.Theme roles + Kirigami.Units with libadwaita named colors, default style, standard 6/12px spacing, CSS style classes; never hardcode colors/fonts — inherit system light/dark/accent via AdwStyleManager. Config schema-driven forms (extension schema, GetConfigSchema) → dynamically built AdwPreferencesGroup: bool→AdwSwitchRow, string→AdwEntryRow (secret→AdwPasswordEntryRow), enum→AdwComboRow, int→AdwSpinRow, with a Save/Apply header action.
interactions: Tap active-watch hero card → open Watch details dialog (bottom sheet mobile / popup desktop).
Connect action on a known-watch row → Connect(name).
Per-watch overflow menu → Re-pair (Repair) / Rename (hook, non-functional until landed) / Forget watch (destructive red → confirm dialog).
Pair new watch (primary action, list-add '+' icon) → PromptDialog 'confirm the 6-digit code on the watch'; closes on ok/error/timeout; confirm-pairing awaits ConfirmPairing(bool).
Ring watch (secondary) → FindWatch(); Sync now (secondary) → re-poll ListWatches.
Firmware banner: Update now → UpdateFirmware + inline FirmwareStatus progress (no detour to Settings); What's new → xdg-open changelogUrl.

Watch details actions: Developer connection, Capture screenshot (TakeScreenshot), Check for updates (CheckFirmware), Language row → picker sub-view (select loads onto watch, current marked), Firmware What's-new link (permanent), Rename, Debug submenu (chevron → second-level view), Forget (red confirm).

Debug submenu items: Core dump, Pull watch logs (GatherLogs), Support bundle (stoandl CLI), Reboot to recovery/PRF (ResetIntoRecovery), Write notification (disabled/SOON), Factory reset (FactoryReset, red confirm).
Apps segmented button group → switch Watchfaces / Apps / Extensions views of one list.

Apps row: tap = launch (LaunchApp; for a face this is set-active); inline gear (if config flag) → OpenConfig → xdg-open; inline bin (if not system) → RemoveApp → confirm 'Remove X? You can reinstall it later'. Inline-button clicks must NOT bubble to the row launch handler.
Install .pbw / Install extension primary action (segment-aware, list-add '+') → FileDialog → SideloadApp/ExtInstall (absolute daemon-side path).

Extensions row: toggle = enabled → ExtEnable/ExtDisable; inline gear (if config) → ExtOpenConfig (url) or schema form; inline bin → ExtUninstall(name, keepConfig) → confirm with 'keep config' checkbox.

Notifications: Master forward toggle; Mute temporarily (30 min / 1 hr / Today); tap per-app row → deeper view (Notifications toggle, Mute temporarily, Vibration pattern radio picker, Custom icon, Allow during quiet hours); Quiet hours Scheduled (from-to toggle) + Quiet now (1 hr / Morning); Filters Add regex filter (allow/block, runs on title+body).

Settings: Sync all now header action; per-service force-sync rows; calendar enable toggles (SetCalendarEnabled); watch settings (quick-launch up/down, backlight, motion backlight, ambient slider); Backup/Restore via stoandl CLI; sub-pages pushed and popped on tab-switch/re-tap of active tab.
Health: read-only; SyncHealth forces a refresh; period/range navigation drives all sections.
Debounce spin/slider writes (a value-changed fires every step and rebuilds the list).
states: ok — normal success.
error — generic failure (surface message tail).
notready — libpebble up but no watch / not ready → the canonical 'no watch connected' empty state.
notfound — target not found.
ambiguous — name matched multiple.
pending — op accepted, awaiting outcome (e.g. Connect may return pending: first).
timeout — op exceeded its poll window (pairing ≤145s, firmware ≤600s, language ≤180s).
inprogress — op running.
reboot — firmware flash terminal (watch reboots, link drops — NOT an error; success = a notready seen AFTER activity).
failed — op terminal failure.
done — op complete (language install).
uptodate — no firmware update available.
disabled / busy / idle / none — service/op-specific states.
confirm:<code> — PairStatus awaiting numeric ConfirmPairing(bool).
Daemon-down — bus name unowned → 'daemon not running' state offering `systemctl --user start stoandl`; nav hidden.
Empty/until-synced — Health before series available (force-sync + last-synced + empty message); HR card hidden entirely if HR not exposed (don't fake).
Loading/in-progress bars — firmware flash and language install progress; pairing dialog awaiting code.
Extension run-state — ready / exited / quarantined (from ExtensionStateChanged), so a crashed-but-enabled ext isn't shown as stale 'running'.
signalsConsumed: Handoff era: NO signals/properties — every live value is polled (focus poll 4s ListWatches+Battery; list refresh on show + after every mutation; Pair 1.5s; Firmware 0.8s; Language 0.6s).

Current (augmenting polling): WatchesChanged → refreshWatches; FirmwareProgress(phase,pct,detail) → push flash progress; LockerChanged → refreshApps; LanguageProgress(phase,pct,detail) → push install progress; ExtensionsChanged → refreshExtensions; ExtensionStateChanged(name,state) → merge per-ext run-state into ExtList rows; CalendarsChanged → refreshCalendars.

Polling remains the fallback because the daemon is NOT D-Bus-activated (a late/reconnecting client can miss a signal): slow safety-net poll + re-sync on daemonUpChanged + op pollers (Pair/Firmware/Language) as watchdogs.
daemonUpChanged (Q_PROPERTY daemonUp) — toggles the daemon-down state / nav visibility and triggers a full re-sync on reconnect.
UI never polls or parses directly — all polling, signal handling, and parsing live in the single StoandlClient shim; QML consumes emitted Qt signals only.
gotchas: Return parsing: split status strings on the FIRST colon only (message tails may contain colons); records are TAB-separated. Parse in the shim layer, never in the UI.
Firmware success is counterintuitive: a `notready` seen AFTER activity = success (watch rebooted, link dropped). Do NOT treat that drop as an error.
Golden rule: the signal/poll is a best-effort poke; ALWAYS re-fetch the screen's list after any mutating call — the re-fetch is authoritative.
Absolute daemon-side paths: everything passed to SideloadApp/SideloadFirmware/ExtInstall/TakeScreenshot must be absolute and resolvable by the daemon (co-located assumption).
sideloaded flag is NOT shown on app rows — stoandl sideloads everything, so the mark is noise. Only active/config/system chips.
For a watchface, tap-to-launch IS set-active (same op) — no separate 'Set as active' item. For an app, tap just runs it.
Inline row action clicks (gear/bin) must be stopped from bubbling to the row's launch handler.
System apps show neither bin (unremovable) nor gear (unless configurable). No 'remove from watch but keep in locker' concept — bin = RemoveApp from the locker (the synced set).

Clay/PKJS + extension config: the GUI only xdg-opens a URL; the daemon's embedded HTTP server handles save. NO webview / scheme handler / QtWebEngine / .desktop handler. WebviewClose(json) is irrelevant (ignore). No completion signal → re-poll on screen refocus.

Extension Configure fans out via config ∈ none|url|schema: url→xdg-open, schema→native form (bool→Switch, string→TextField[secret→password], enum→ComboBox, int→SpinBox), none→no Configure action. Don't fake settings UI before the hook lands.
Debounce number/slider writes: onValueChanged fires every step and applyPref rebuilds the whole list.

Mobile-vs-desktop in Kirigami is PLATFORM/INPUT-driven (Settings.isMobile), NOT window size — resizing a desktop window does NOT reflow the action. In GTK/libadwaita this becomes SIZE-driven (AdwBreakpoint / AdwViewSwitcher policy), so drop any isMobile concept and drive layout off breakpoints.

The prototype's bottom-right round '+' FAB is a Material idiom, NOT a KDE (or GNOME) pattern — IGNORE it; use page actions in the header. When prototype and platform convention disagree, platform convention wins (carries to GNOME: no FAB, header + button).
Never hardcode colors/fonts — the prototype's dark hexes are a DENSITY/LAYOUT spec, not a color spec. Inherit the system light/dark/accent scheme; hardcoding breaks adaptation.
Danger-zone actions (Forget watch, Factory reset, Uninstall/Remove) are destructive-red and always behind a confirm dialog.
Serial and Board values are rendered monospaced in the Watch details rows.
Charging state is unavailable at the hardware level — do NOT design UI for it; battery/state refresh only on the focus poll.
notready is a first-class empty state (no watch / not ready), distinct from an error — handle it explicitly everywhere a watch is required.

Feature/nav history: Extensions was folded into Apps as a 3rd segment; Notifications was promoted to its own screen; Sync + System merged into Settings, then firmware/language/diagnostics/danger-zone were moved OUT of Settings (firmware→Watch banner+details, language→Watch details, logs/support/core-dump/PRF/factory-reset→Watch Debug submenu); Settings later became a category landing of sub-pages; Calendars moved from a flat list in Sync into their own page when account grouping + CRUD landed (CalDAV password field write-only, blank = keep); the HARDWARE list and standalone Firmware row were dropped as duplicates — do NOT re-add.

The drift-report loop is the process contract: after each milestone report D-Bus contract deltas, missing daemon surface, real-device UX findings, decisions, and screenshots — keeping prototype ↔ handoff ↔ build in sync.
